title.zh: 卷一百二十九 志第八十二 樂四
title.raw: 卷一百二十九 志第八十二 樂四 Volume 129 Treatises 82: Music 4

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年七月，鑄帝鼐、八鼎成。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Chongning, the casting of the Emperor's Ding and the Eight Tripod Cauldrons was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chongning 4, the Emperor's great pitch-tripod and the eight ritual cauldrons were cast and finished.

sentences.zh: 八月，大司樂劉昺言：“大朝會宮架舊用十二熊羆按，金錞、簫、鼓、觱篥等與大樂合奏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Director of Music Liu Bing said: "At grand court assemblies the palace orchestral stands formerly used the twelve bear-and-panda formations, with metal clappers, xiao flutes, drums, bili oboes, and the like performing together with the great music."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Liu Bing, Director of Music, memorialized: "At great court assemblies the palace stands had long employed the twelve-section bear-and-panda battery, with metal clappers, vertical flutes, drums, double-reed pipes, and similar instruments joining in with the great music."

sentences.zh: 今所造大樂，遠稽古製，不應雜以鄭、衛。

translations.literal: "The great music now being created looks far back to ancient institutions and should not be mixed with Zheng and Wei music."
translations.idiomatic: "The great music now being fashioned reaches deep into antiquity; it ought not be adulterated with the sounds of Zheng and Wei."

sentences.zh: ”詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered this discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that practice abolished.

sentences.zh: 又依昺改定二舞，各九成，每三成為一變，執籥秉翟，揚戈持盾，威儀之節，以象治功。

translations.literal: Also, following Bing's revisions, the two ritual dances were each set in nine segments, every three segments forming one transformation; holding yue flutes and bearing pheasant feathers, brandishing halberds and bearing shields—the ritual postures symbolized the achievements of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Bing also revised the two dances so that each had nine segments, three segments per transformation; performers held flutes and feather staffs, raised halberds and carried shields—every gesture in the ceremonial pattern stood for the work of good government.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，樂成，列於崇政殿。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day the music was completed and displayed in the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin the music was finished and set out in the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 有旨，先奏舊樂三闕，曲未終，帝曰：“舊樂如泣聲。

translations.literal: There was an order to play the old music first for three movements; before the pieces ended, the Emperor said: "The old music sounds like weeping."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the old music played first for three movements; before the airs finished, the Emperor said, "This old music sounds like lamentation."

sentences.zh: ”揮止之。

translations.literal: He waved to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: He gestured for it to cease.

sentences.zh: 既奏新樂，天顏和豫，百僚稱頌。

translations.literal: After the new music was performed, the Emperor's countenance was serene and pleased, and the hundred officials offered praise.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new music had been played, the Emperor's face brightened with ease, and the officials all extolled it.

sentences.zh: 九月朔，以鼎樂成，帝御大慶殿受賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, because the tripod music was complete, the Emperor took his seat in the Daqing Hall to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the ninth month, with the tripod music complete, the Emperor presided in the Daqing Hall to receive felicitations.

sentences.zh: 是日，初用新樂，太尉率百僚奉觴稱壽，有數鶴從東北來，飛度黃庭，回翔鳴唳。

translations.literal: That day the new music was used for the first time; the Grand Marshal led the hundred officials in offering the cup and wishing long life, and several cranes came from the northeast, flying across the Imperial Court and circling overhead with cries.
translations.idiomatic: That day the new music was heard for the first time. The Grand Marshal led the officials in raising the longevity cup, while several cranes flew in from the northeast, passed over the Yellow Court, and wheeled aloft, calling as they went.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：“禮樂之興，百年於此。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued, saying: "The rise of ritual and music—such a thing comes only once in a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "The flourishing of ritual and music is an event that comes once in a century.

sentences.zh: 然去聖愈遠，遺聲弗存。

translations.literal: Yet the farther we are from the sages, the less their sounds survive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the more distant we grow from the sages, the less their music remains.

sentences.zh: 乃者，得隱逸之士於草茅之賤，獲《英莖》之器於受命之邦。

translations.literal: Recently a reclusive scholar was found among humble commoners, and the Yingjing instrument was obtained in the land where the Mandate was received.
translations.idiomatic: Of late a hidden scholar emerged from the humblest ranks, and the Yingjing pitch-vessel was recovered in the state that received the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 適時之宜，以身為度，鑄鼎以起律，因律以製器，按協於庭，八音克諧。

translations.literal: Suited to the times, taking the body as the measure, casting tripods to establish pitch pipes and from the pipes making instruments—harmonized in the courtyard, the eight tones achieved concord.
translations.idiomatic: Fitting the moment, using the body as standard, casting tripods to fix the pitch pipes and shaping instruments from those pipes, all were tuned in the court until the eight sounds were in harmony.

sentences.zh: 昔堯有《大章》，舜有《大韶》，三代之王亦各異名。

translations.literal: In antiquity Yao had the "Great Pattern," Shun the "Great Shao," and the kings of the Three Dynasties each had different names as well.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Yao had the Great Zhang, Shun the Great Shao, and the kings of the Three Dynasties likewise each bore a distinct name.

sentences.zh: 今追千載而成一代之製，宜賜新樂之名曰《大晟》，朕將薦郊廟、享鬼神、和萬邦，與天下共之。

translations.literal: Now, tracing a thousand years to complete the institutions of a single age, the new music should be granted the name "Great Sheng"; I shall offer it at the suburban altars, present it to the spirits, harmonize the myriad states, and share it with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after a millennium, the music of one age is complete. Let the new music be named the Great Sheng. I shall present it at the suburban altars, offer it to the spirits, harmonize the myriad realms, and share it with the world.

sentences.zh: 其舊樂勿用。

translations.literal: The old music is not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: The former music must no longer be performed.

translations.literal: " (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 先是，端州上古銅器，有樂鍾，驗其窾識，乃宋成公時。

translations.literal: Previously, in Duanzhou ancient bronze vessels were found, including a musical bell; examining its inscription, they were from the time of Duke Cheng of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, ancient bronzes turned up in Duanzhou, among them a ritual bell; inspection of the inscription showed they dated to Duke Cheng of Song.

sentences.zh: 帝以端王繼大統，故詔言受命之邦，而隱逸之士謂漢津也。

translations.literal: Because the Emperor had succeeded to the Great Succession as Prince of Duan, the edict spoke of "the land where the Mandate was received," while the reclusive scholar referred to Wei Hanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Emperor had inherited the throne from his tenure as Prince of Duan, the edict spoke of the state that received the Mandate, whereas the hidden scholar meant Wei Hanjin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷舊以禮樂掌於太常，至是專置大晟府，大司樂一員、典樂二員並為長貳，大樂令一員、協律郎四員，又有制撰官，為製甚備，於是禮、樂始分為二。

translations.literal: The court had formerly entrusted ritual and music to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; now a Great Sheng Prefecture was established specifically, with one Director of Music and two Directors of Ceremonial Music as chief officers, one Superintendent of Great Music and four Masters of Temperament, plus composition officers—the arrangement was very complete, and thus ritual and music were first divided into two separate administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music had long been overseen by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; now a Great Sheng Prefecture was set up on its own, with one Director of Music and two Superintendents of Music as heads, one Superintendent of Great Music and four Regulation Masters, along with composers—the organization was fully in place, and ritual and music were at last separated.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，詔曰：“樂不作久矣！

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, an edict said: "Music has long gone unmade!
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 5, an edict declared: "Music has not been properly fashioned for ages!

sentences.zh: 朕承先誌，述而作之，以追先王之緒；

translations.literal: I have inherited the prior design and, composing anew, seek to follow the thread of the former kings;
translations.idiomatic: Following the intent of my predecessors, I compose anew to recover the legacy of the ancient kings;

sentences.zh: 建官分屬，設府庀徒，以成一代之製。

translations.literal: establishing offices and dividing responsibilities, setting up a prefecture and gathering craftsmen, to complete the institutions of a single age.
translations.idiomatic: creating offices, assigning duties, founding a bureau and mustering artisans, thereby completing the music of our age.

sentences.zh: 二月，嚐詔省內外冗官，大晟府亦並之禮官。

translations.literal: In the second month an edict had ordered the reduction of redundant offices inside and outside the court, and the Great Sheng Prefecture was also merged into the ritual offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict had cut superfluous posts throughout the government, and the Great Sheng Prefecture too was folded into the ritual administration.

sentences.zh: 夫舜命夔典樂，命伯夷典禮，禮樂異道，各分所守，豈可同職？

translations.literal: When Shun charged Kui with music and Boyi with ritual, ritual and music were different paths, each with its own charge—how could they share one office?
translations.idiomatic: Shun appointed Kui to oversee music and Boyi to oversee ritual; ritual and music are distinct duties, each with its own keeper—how could one man hold both?

sentences.zh: 其大晟府名可復仍舊。

translations.literal: The name Great Sheng Prefecture may be restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let the title Great Sheng Prefecture be reinstated as it was.

translations.literal: " (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：“樂作已久，方薦之郊廟，施於朝廷，而未及頒之天下。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Music has long been made, and is about to be presented at the suburban altars and employed at court, yet it has not been distributed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "Our music has been ready for some time and is offered at the altars and performed at court, but it has not yet been sent out to the empire.

sentences.zh: 宜令大晟府議頒新樂，使雅正之聲被於四海，先降三京四輔，次帥府。

translations.literal: The Great Sheng Prefecture should deliberate on distributing the new music so that correct and proper sounds reach the four seas, first to the three capitals and four auxiliary prefectures, then to the military commission prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Great Sheng Prefecture plan the dissemination of the new music so that upright sounds spread across the realm—first to the three capitals and four adjunct districts, then to the commandery seats.

translations.literal: " (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，詔曰：“自唐以來，正聲全失，無徵角之音，五聲不備，豈足以道和而化俗哉？

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, an edict said: "Since the Tang, the correct tones have been wholly lost; there are no zhi or jiao notes, and the five tones are incomplete—how can this suffice to harmonize the Way and transform custom?
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 2 an edict stated: "From the Tang onward the orthodox scale has been utterly lost: the zhi and jiao pitches are missing and the five tones are incomplete—how can such music guide the Way and reform society?"

sentences.zh: 劉詵所上徵聲，可令大晟府同教坊依譜按習，仍增徵、角二譜，候習熟來上。

translations.literal: The zhi tones submitted by Liu Shen may be taught by the Great Sheng Prefecture together with the Music Office according to the score; the zhi and jiao registers should also be expanded, and when practice is proficient they are to be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Let the zhi music that Liu Shen presented be rehearsed at the Great Sheng Prefecture and the Music Office according to the notation; add registers for the zhi and jiao modes, and when training is complete submit them.

sentences.zh: ”初，進士彭幾進樂書，論五音，言本朝以火德王，而羽音不禁，徵調尚闕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the jinshi Peng Ji had submitted a book on music discussing the five tones, saying that our dynasty rules by the Fire Virtue yet the yu tone is not restrained and the zhi mode is still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: At first the presented scholar Peng Ji had offered a treatise on the five tones, arguing that since the dynasty holds the Fire Virtue the yu pitch ought to be checked and the zhi mode was still absent.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎吳時善其說，建言乞召幾至樂府，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Wu Shi, an aide in the Ministry of Rites, approved his theory and memorialized asking that Ji be summoned to the Music Office; the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shi of the Ministry of Rites endorsed the proposal and asked that Ji be called to the music bureau; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 至是，詵亦上徵聲，乃降是詔。

translations.literal: By this time Shen too had submitted zhi music, and so this edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shen also presented zhi music, and hence this edict.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，詔：“今學校所用，不過春秋釋奠，如賜宴辟雍，乃用鄭、衛之音，雜以俳優之戲，非所以示多士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, an edict said: "What the schools use today goes no further than the spring and autumn sacrifices to the sage; yet at banquets in the Imperial Academy they employ Zheng and Wei music mixed with comic actors—this is not how to set an example for the many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 3 an edict said: "Schools nowadays use music only for the seasonal sacrifices to the sage; yet at Imperial Academy feasts they still play Zheng and Wei airs interlaced with comic performances—hardly a model for cultivated gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 其自今用雅樂。

translations.literal: From now on let elegant music be used.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth let proper court music be used.

translations.literal: " (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 四年四月，議禮局言：“國家崇奉感生帝、神州地祇為大祠，以僖祖、太祖配侑，而有司行事不設宮架、二舞，殊失所以尊祖、侑神作主之意。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, the Ritual Deliberation Bureau said: "The state honors the Regenerative Emperor and the Earth Spirit of the Nine Regions as great sacrifices, with the Exalted Ancestor and Taizu as spirit partners, yet the officiants do not set up palace orchestral stands or the two dances—this greatly fails to express the intent of honoring the ancestors and enshrining the spirits as hosts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 4 the Ritual Deliberation Bureau reported: "The state venerates the Regenerative Emperor and the Earth Spirit as major rites, with the Exalted Ancestor and Taizu as co-recipients, yet the officers perform them without palace stands or the two dances—far short of the meaning of honoring forebears and pairing the gods."

sentences.zh: 乞皆用宮架、二舞。

translations.literal: We ask that palace stands and the two dances be used in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: We request that palace stands and both dances be used throughout.

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted the request.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔近選國子生教習二舞，以備祠祀先聖，本《周官》教國子之製。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an edict ordered that students of the National University recently selected be taught the two dances to prepare for sacrifices to the sage—this followed the Zhou regulation for instructing the sons of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict directed that newly chosen National University students be trained in the two dances for rites to the sage, following the Zhou practice of educating the royal sons.

sentences.zh: 然士子肄業上庠，頗聞恥於樂舞與樂工為伍、坐作、進退。

translations.literal: Yet gentlemen studying in the upper academy were widely heard to be ashamed of dancing alongside musicians, of sitting and rising and advancing and retreating with them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scholars at the upper academy were said to feel shame at performing dance alongside musicians, sharing their postures of sitting, rising, advancing, and withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 蓋今古異時，致於古雖有其跡，施於今未適其宜。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern times differ; though the ancient practice survives in form, applying it today does not suit the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Times have changed: though the ancient trace remains, imposing it now is ill-suited.

sentences.zh: 其罷習二舞，願習雅樂者聽。

translations.literal: Let training in the two dances be discontinued; those who wish to study elegant music may do so.
translations.idiomatic: Discontinue the two-dance training; those who wish to study court music may.

translations.literal: " (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 八月，帝親製《大晟樂記》，命太中大夫劉昺編修《樂書》，為八論：

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Emperor personally composed the "Record of Great Sheng Music" and ordered the Grand Master for All-Pervasive Governance Liu Bing to compile the "Book of Music" in eight treatises:
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Emperor wrote the Record of Great Sheng Music himself and ordered Liu Bing to edit the Book of Music in eight sections:

sentences.zh: 其一曰：樂由陽來，陽之數極於九，聖人攝其數於九鼎，寓其聲於九成。

translations.literal: The first says: Music arises from yang; the number of yang culminates in nine. The sage gathers that number in the Nine Tripods and lodges its sound in the nine segments.
translations.idiomatic: The first: Music comes from yang; yang's number reaches its limit at nine. The sage concentrates that number in the nine tripods and embodies its sound in nine segments.

sentences.zh: 陽之數復而為一，則寶鼎之卦為《坎》；

translations.literal: When yang's number returns and becomes one, the hexagram of the precious tripod is Kan;
translations.idiomatic: When yang's number cycles back to one, the trigram of the precious tripod is Kan;

sentences.zh: 極而為九，則彤鼎之卦為《離》。

translations.literal: when it culminates in nine, the hexagram of the red tripod is Li.
translations.idiomatic: when it reaches nine, the trigram of the red tripod is Li.

sentences.zh: 《離》，南方之卦也。

translations.literal: Li is the trigram of the south.
translations.idiomatic: Li is the southern trigram.

sentences.zh: 聖人以光明盛大之業，如日方中，向明而治，故極九之數則曰景鍾，大樂之名則曰《大晟》。

translations.literal: The sage, with a brilliant and grand enterprise like the sun at midday, facing the light to govern—therefore when the number reaches nine it is called the Splendid Bell, and the name of the great music is the "Great Sheng."
translations.idiomatic: The sage's radiant and vast undertaking is like the sun at noon, governing toward the light; hence at the number nine the bell is called the Splendid Bell, and the great music is named the Great Sheng.

sentences.zh: 日王於午，火明於南，乘火德之運。

translations.literal: The sun rules at wu, fire shines in the south, riding the fortune of the Fire Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The sun holds sway at noon, fire blazes in the south—we ride the destiny of Fire.

sentences.zh: 當豐大之時，恢擴規模，增光前烈，明盛之業，永觀厥成。

translations.literal: In a time of abundance and greatness, expanding the scale and adding luster to former glory—the brilliant enterprise may long be viewed as achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of fullness and magnitude we enlarge the design and brighten past glory, that this splendid achievement may endure.

sentences.zh: 樂名《大晟》，不亦宜乎？

translations.literal: Is not the name "Great Sheng" fitting?
translations.idiomatic: What name could suit better than the Great Sheng?

sentences.zh: 其二曰：後世以黍定律，其失樂之本也遠矣。

translations.literal: The second says: Later ages used millet to fix pitch pipes—a departure very far from the root of music.
translations.idiomatic: The second: Later generations used millet grains to set the pitch pipes, straying far from music's foundation.

sentences.zh: 以黍定尺，起於西漢，蓋承《六經》散亡之後，聞古人之緒餘而執以為法，聲既未協，乃屢變其法而求之。

translations.literal: Using millet to fix the foot-measure began in the Western Han, likely because after the Six Classics were scattered one clung to remnants of the ancients as law; the tones were not yet concordant, so the method was repeatedly changed in search of them.
translations.idiomatic: Fixing the measure by millet began in Western Han, probably because after the classics were lost men seized on surviving traces of antiquity as standard; when the pitches still failed to agree, they altered the method again and again.

sentences.zh: 此古今之尺所以至於數十等，而至和之聲愈求而不可得也。

translations.literal: This is why ancient and modern foot-measures have come to several dozen grades, yet the more one seeks the sound of perfect harmony, the less it can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Thus measures ancient and modern have multiplied into dozens of variants, while perfect harmony grows ever harder to find.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：“萬物皆備於我矣，反身而誠，樂莫大焉！

translations.literal: The Classic says: "The myriad things are all prepared in me; turn inward in sincerity and there is no greater joy!
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "All things are complete within me; turn inward in sincerity—what greater joy than this!

sentences.zh: ”黍雲乎哉？

translations.literal: What need of millet?
translations.idiomatic: Need we speak of millet?

sentences.zh: 其三曰：焦急之聲不可用於隆盛之世。

translations.literal: The third says: Hurried and pressing sounds cannot be used in an age of grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: The third: Hasty, strained music cannot serve a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 昔李照欲下其律，乃曰：“異日聽吾樂，當令人物舒長。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Zhao wished to lower the pitch and said: "Another day when you hear my music, you will find people relaxed and at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Zhao proposed lowering the pitch, saying, "When you hear my music hereafter, you will see men calm and unhurried."

sentences.zh: ”照之樂固未足以感動和氣如此，然亦不可謂無其意矣。

translations.literal: Zhao's music was indeed not enough to move harmonious qi to such a degree, yet one cannot say he had no such intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's music could hardly stir harmonious breath to that extent, yet he was not without the idea.

sentences.zh: 自藝祖禦極，和樂之聲高，曆一百五十餘年，而後中正之聲乃定。

translations.literal: From the time our Founder took the throne, harmonious music was high-pitched; more than a hundred and fifty years passed before the correct central tones were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Since our founding emperor's accession the pitch of harmonious music had been high; only after more than a century and a half were the true central tones settled.

sentences.zh: 蓋奕世修德，和氣薰蒸，一代之樂，理若有待。

translations.literal: For generations virtue was cultivated and harmonious qi steamed upward—the music of an age, it seems, waits upon its time.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation refined virtue until harmonious qi ripened; the music of an era, it seems, must await its moment.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：盛古帝王皆以明堂為先務，後世知為崇配、布政之宮，然要妙之旨，秘而不傳，徒區區於形製之末流，而不知帝王之所以用心也。

translations.literal: The fourth says: The great ancient emperors all made the Bright Hall their first task; later ages knew it as the palace for honoring Heaven and issuing government, yet the essential subtlety was kept secret and not transmitted—they fussed over outward forms while not knowing where the emperors placed their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: Ancient kings all placed the Bright Hall foremost; later men knew it as the hall for matching Heaven and proclaiming policy, yet its subtle core was never handed down—men squabbled over outward form without grasping the sovereign's true concern.

sentences.zh: 且盛德在木，則居青陽，角聲乃作；

translations.literal: When flourishing virtue resides in wood, one dwells in the Green Yang quarter and the jiao tone is performed;
translations.idiomatic: When virtue flourishes in wood, one abides in the Green Yang pavilion and the jiao pitch sounds;

sentences.zh: 盛德在火，則居明堂，徵聲乃作；

translations.literal: when flourishing virtue resides in fire, one dwells in the Bright Hall and the zhi tone is performed;
translations.idiomatic: when virtue flourishes in fire, one abides in the Bright Hall and the zhi pitch sounds;

sentences.zh: 盛德在金，則居總章，商聲乃作；

translations.literal: when flourishing virtue resides in metal, one dwells in the Total Manifestation quarter and the shang tone is performed;
translations.idiomatic: when virtue flourishes in metal, one abides in the Total Manifestation hall and the shang pitch sounds;

sentences.zh: 盛德在水，則居玄堂，羽聲乃作；

translations.literal: when flourishing virtue resides in water, one dwells in the Dark Hall and the yu tone is performed;
translations.idiomatic: when virtue flourishes in water, one abides in the Dark Hall and the yu pitch sounds;

sentences.zh: 盛德在土，則居中央，宮聲乃作。

translations.literal: when flourishing virtue resides in earth, one dwells in the center and the gong tone is performed.
translations.idiomatic: when virtue flourishes in earth, one abides at the center and the gong pitch sounds.

sentences.zh: 其應時之妙，不可勝言。

translations.literal: Its responsiveness to the seasons cannot be fully described.
translations.idiomatic: Its attunement to the seasons defies full description.

sentences.zh: 一歲之中，兼總五運，凡麗於五行者，以聲召氣，無不總攝。

translations.literal: Within a year the five movements are all embraced; whatever pertains to the Five Phases summons qi by sound, and nothing escapes harmonization.
translations.idiomatic: Through the year all five movements are gathered; whatever belongs to the Five Phases is summoned by pitch, and nothing lies outside their embrace.

sentences.zh: 鼓宮宮動，鼓角角應：彼亦莫知所以使之者。

translations.literal: Strike the gong and the gong pipes resonate; strike the jiao and the jiao pipes respond—neither knows what makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Beat the gong tone and the gong pipes stir; beat the jiao and the jiao pipes answer—yet none can say who moves them.

sentences.zh: 則永膺壽考，曆數過期，不亦宜乎？

translations.literal: Then long life and a reign beyond counting—is this not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Then enduring life and a mandate without end—would that not be meet?

sentences.zh: 其五曰：魏漢津以太極元氣，函三為一，九寸之律，三數退藏，故八寸七分為中聲。

translations.literal: The fifth says: Wei Hanjin took the primordial qi of the Great Ultimate, enclosing three as one; the nine-inch pitch pipe with three numbers retreating and stored yields eight inches and seven tenths as the central tone.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth: Wei Hanjin held that the Great Ultimate's primordial breath unites three into one; the nine-inch pipe, with three numbers withdrawn and stored, gives eight and seven-tenths inches as the central pitch.

sentences.zh: 正聲得正氣則用之，中聲得中氣則用之。

translations.literal: The correct tone uses correct qi; the central tone uses central qi.
translations.idiomatic: Proper pitch employs proper breath; the median pitch employs median breath.

sentences.zh: 宮架環列，以應十二辰；

translations.literal: Palace stands arrayed in a ring to correspond to the twelve double-hours;
translations.idiomatic: Palace stands ring the hall to answer the twelve earthly branches;

sentences.zh: 中正之聲，以應二十四氣；

translations.literal: correct central tones to correspond to the twenty-four qi periods;
translations.idiomatic: the true central pitches answer the twenty-four seasonal nodes;

sentences.zh: 加四清聲，以應二十八宿。

translations.literal: adding the four clear tones to correspond to the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
translations.idiomatic: four clear tones are added to match the twenty-eight lodges.

sentences.zh: 氣不頓進，八音乃諧。

translations.literal: When qi does not rush forward, the eight tones are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: If breath does not leap ahead abruptly, the eight sounds harmonize.

sentences.zh: 若立春在歲元之後，則迎其氣而用之，餘悉隨氣用律，使無過不及之差，則所以感召陰陽之和，其法不亦密乎？

translations.literal: If Beginning of Spring falls after the year's origin, welcome that qi and use it; the rest all follow qi in applying pitch pipes, so there is no excess or shortfall—then the method of summoning the harmony of yin and yang is not precise indeed?
translations.idiomatic: When Beginning of Spring comes after the year's start, greet that breath and apply it; all else follows the seasonal breath in choosing pipes, neither overshooting nor falling short—is not this a subtle way to call forth the harmony of yin and yang?

sentences.zh: 其六曰：乾坤交於亥，而子生於黃鍾之宮，故稟於乾，交於亥，任於壬，生於子。

translations.literal: The sixth says: Qian and Kun meet at hai, and zi is born in the palace of the Yellow Bell; thus endowed from Qian, meeting at hai, acting at ren, born at zi.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth: Qian and Kun join at hai, and zi is born in the Yellow Bell palace—endowed from Qian, meeting at hai, operating at ren, born at zi.

sentences.zh: 自乾至子凡四位，而清聲具焉。

translations.literal: From Qian to zi are four positions in all, and the clear tones are complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: From Qian to zi span four stations, and within them the clear tones are complete.

sentences.zh: 漢津以四清為至陽之氣，在二十八宿為虛、昴、星、房，四者居四方之正位，以統十二律。

translations.literal: Hanjin took the four clear tones as the utmost yang qi; among the twenty-eight lodges they are Void, Pleiades, Star, and Room—four occupying the cardinal directions to govern the twelve pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin regarded the four clear tones as supreme yang breath; among the twenty-eight lodges they are Void, Pleiades, Star, and Room—each at a cardinal point governing the twelve pipes.

sentences.zh: 每清聲皆有三統：申、子、辰屬於虛而統於子，巳、酉、醜屬於昴而統於醜，寅、午、戌屬於星而統於寅，亥、卯、未屬於房而統於卯。

translations.literal: Each clear tone has three affiliations: shen, zi, and chen belong to Void and are governed by zi; si, you, and chou belong to Pleiades and are governed by chou; yin, wu, and xu belong to Star and are governed by yin; hai, mao, and wei belong to Room and are governed by mao.
translations.idiomatic: Each clear tone commands three groups: shen-zi-chen fall under Void and are ruled by zi; si-you-chou under Pleiades by chou; yin-wu-xu under Star by yin; hai-mao-wei under Room by mao.

sentences.zh: 中正之聲分為二十四宿，統於四清焉。

translations.literal: The correct central tones are divided among the twenty-four lodges and governed by the four clear tones.
translations.idiomatic: The true central pitches are apportioned to the twenty-four lodges and ruled by the four clear tones.

sentences.zh: 其七曰：昔人以樂之器有時而弊，故律失則求之於鍾，鍾失則求之於鼎，得一鼎之龠，則權衡度量可考而知。

translations.literal: The seventh says: Men of old thought musical instruments wear out in time, so when pitch pipes failed they sought bells, and when bells failed they sought tripods; obtaining one tripod pitch-tube, weights and measures could be examined and known.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh: Ancients believed instruments decay with time; when pipes failed they turned to bells, when bells failed to tripods—one tripod tube yielded measurable weights and lengths.

sentences.zh: 故鼎以全渾淪之體，律呂以達陰陽之情，天地之間，無不統攝，機緘運用，萬物振作，則樂之感人，豈無所自而然耶？

translations.literal: Thus the tripod embodies the whole undifferentiated body, pitch pipes express the feelings of yin and yang—between Heaven and Earth nothing escapes harmonization; as the pivot turns and the myriad things stir, can music move people without cause?
translations.idiomatic: The tripod holds the undivided whole, pipes voice yin and yang—nothing under heaven lies outside their sway; as the mechanism turns and all things quicken, how could music touch the heart without origin?

sentences.zh: 其八曰：聖上稽帝王之製而成一代之樂，以謂帝舜之樂以教胄子，乃頒之於宗學。

translations.literal: The eighth says: The sage traced the institutions of emperors and kings to complete the music of a single age, holding that Emperor Shun's music taught the crown princes—therefore it was distributed to the clan schools.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth: Our sovereign reviewed the kings' models to finish the music of the age, judging that Shun's music educated the royal heirs—so it was sent to the clan academies.

sentences.zh: 成周之樂，掌於成均，乃頒之府學、辟雍、太學；

translations.literal: The music of accomplished Zhou was held at the Chengjun, and was distributed to the prefectural schools, the Imperial Academy, and the National University;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's perfected music resided at the Chengjun and was issued to prefectural schools, the Imperial Academy, and the National University;

sentences.zh: 而三京藩邸，凡祭祀之用樂者皆賜之，於是中正之聲被天下矣。

translations.literal: and the three capitals and princely establishments—wherever sacrifice required music—all received it; thus correct central sounds covered the realm.
translations.idiomatic: the three capitals and princely residences, and every place that used music in sacrifice—all received it, until upright tones filled the world.

sentences.zh: 漢施鄭聲於朝廷，唐升夷部於堂上，至於房中之樂，唯恐淫哇之聲變態之不新也。

translations.literal: Han introduced Zheng music at court, Tang elevated barbarian airs in the hall, and even for inner-chamber music they feared that licentious sounds would not change and grow novel enough.
translations.idiomatic: The Han brought Zheng music into court, the Tang raised foreign suites to the hall; even private chamber music they dreaded might not grow fresh in wanton novelty.

sentences.zh: 聖上樂聞平淡之音，而特詔有司製為宮架，施之於禁庭，房中用雅樂，自今朝始雲。

translations.literal: The sage delights in plain and tranquil tones and specially ordered officials to make palace stands for the forbidden precinct; elegant music is used in the inner chambers—from this court onward.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign loves plain, tranquil sounds and commanded palace stands for the inner court; proper music now serves the private apartments—beginning with this reign.

sentences.zh: 又為圖十二：一曰五聲，二曰八音，三曰十二律應二十八宿，四曰七均應二十八宿，五曰八十四調，六曰十二律所生，七曰十二律應二十四氣，八曰十二律鍾正聲，九曰堂上樂，十曰金鍾玉磬，十一曰宮架，十二曰二舞。

translations.literal: Twelve diagrams were also made: (1) the five tones, (2) the eight sounds, (3) the twelve pitch pipes corresponding to the twenty-eight lodges, (4) the seven scales corresponding to the twenty-eight lodges, (5) the eighty-four modes, (6) what the twelve pipes generate, (7) the twelve pipes corresponding to the twenty-four qi, (8) the twelve pipes and bell correct tones, (9) hall music, (10) metal bells and jade chimes, (11) palace stands, (12) the two dances.
translations.idiomatic: He also commissioned twelve charts: the five tones; the eight sounds; twelve pipes against the twenty-eight lodges; seven scales against the lodges; eighty-four modes; generations of the twelve pipes; pipes against the twenty-four qi; pipes and bell orthodox pitches; hall music; gold bells and jade stones; palace stands; and the two dances.

sentences.zh: 圖雖不能具載，觀其所序，亦可以知其旨意矣：

translations.literal: Though the diagrams cannot all be recorded here, from their arrangement one may grasp the intent:
translations.idiomatic: The charts cannot all be reproduced here, yet from their order one may discern the design:

sentences.zh: 天地相合，五數乃備，不動者為五位，常動者為五行，五行發而為五聲。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth combine and the number five is complete; the unmoving are the five positions, the ever-moving the Five Phases; the Five Phases issue forth as the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth unite and the number five is whole: the static are the five positions, the active the Five Phases; from the Five Phases arise the five tones.

sentences.zh: 律呂相生，五聲乃備，布於十二律之間，猶五緯往還於十有二次，五運斡旋於十有二時。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes beget one another and the five tones are complete, distributed among the twelve pitch pipes like the five planets cycling through the twelve stations, the Five Movements turning through the twelve double-hours.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes generate one another until the five tones are full, set among the twelve pitches as the five luminaries wheel through twelve stations, the Five Movements revolving through twelve hours.

sentences.zh: 其圖五聲以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the five tones is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart for the five tones.

sentences.zh: 兩儀既判，八卦肇分。

translations.literal: Once the Two Principles had been demarcated, the Eight Trigrams first divided.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Principles were set apart, the Eight Trigrams first took shape.

sentences.zh: 氣盈而動，八風行焉。

translations.literal: When qi was full it moved, and the eight winds came into motion.
translations.idiomatic: When breath brimmed full it stirred, and the eight winds began to blow.

sentences.zh: 顓帝乃令飛龍效八風之音，命之曰《承雲》。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanxu then ordered Feilong to imitate the sounds of the eight winds, naming it "Receiving the Clouds."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanxu had Feilong imitate the eight winds and named the piece "Receiving the Clouds."

sentences.zh: 方是時，金、石、絲、竹、匏、土、革、木之音未備，後聖有作，以八方之物全五聲者，製而為八音，以聲召氣，八風從律。

translations.literal: At that time the sounds of metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, leather, and wood were not yet complete; later sages arose and, using things of the eight directions to complete the five tones, fashioned them into the eight sounds; by sound they summoned qi, and the eight winds followed the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In that age the tones of metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, clay, hide, and wood were not yet whole; later sages took materials from the eight quarters to fill out the five tones, fashioned the eight sounds, and by pitch summoned breath until the eight winds answered the pipes.

sentences.zh: 其圖八音以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the eight sounds is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart for the eight sounds.

sentences.zh: 上象著明器形，而下以聲召氣，吻合元精。

translations.literal: Above, shapes made the forms of instruments manifest and clear; below, by sound qi was summoned—matching the primordial essence.
translations.idiomatic: Above, it shows the bright forms of the instruments; below, pitch summons breath and joins the primordial essence.

sentences.zh: 其圖十二律應二十八宿以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the twelve pitch pipes corresponding to the twenty-eight lodges is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart of the twelve pipes against the twenty-eight lodges.

sentences.zh: 鬥在天中，周製四方，猶宮聲處中為四聲之綱。

translations.literal: The Dipper is at heaven's center, governing the four directions round about, just as the gong tone at the center is the guide of the four tones.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper stands at heaven's center and wheels the four quarters, as the gong pitch at the center guides the other four tones.

sentences.zh: 二十八舍列在四方，用之於合樂者，蓋樂方七角屬木，南方七徵屬火，西方七商屬金，北方七羽屬水。

translations.literal: The twenty-eight lodges are arrayed in the four directions; as used in combined music, the eastern seven jiao belong to wood, the southern seven zhi to fire, the western seven shang to metal, and the northern seven yu to water.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight lodges stand in the four quarters; in ensemble music the eastern seven jiao appertain to wood, the southern seven zhi to fire, the western seven shang to metal, and the northern seven yu to water.

sentences.zh: 四方之宿各有所屬，而每方之中，七均備足。

translations.literal: Each lodge of the four directions has its own affiliation, and within each direction the seven jun are fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: Every lodge in each quarter has its proper assignment, and within each quarter all seven scale degrees are complete.

sentences.zh: 中央七宮管攝四氣。

translations.literal: The seven gong at the center govern the four qi.
translations.idiomatic: The seven gong at the center oversee the four seasonal breaths.

sentences.zh: 故二十八舍應中正之聲者，製器之法也；

translations.literal: Thus the twenty-eight lodges corresponding to correct central tones are the method of making instruments;
translations.idiomatic: Hence matching the twenty-eight lodges to the true central pitches is the art of fashioning instruments;

sentences.zh: 二十八舍應七均之聲者，和聲之術也。

translations.literal: the twenty-eight lodges corresponding to the seven jun tones are the technique of harmonizing sounds.
translations.idiomatic: matching them to the seven scale degrees is the art of blending tones.

sentences.zh: 其圖七均應二十八宿以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the seven jun corresponding to the twenty-eight lodges is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart of the seven scales against the twenty-eight lodges.

sentences.zh: 合陰陽之聲而文之以五聲，則九六相交，均聲乃備。

translations.literal: Combining yin and yang sounds and patterning them with the five tones, then nine and six intercross and the jun tones are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Join yin and yang pitches and adorn them with the five tones—nine and six cross, and the scale degrees are whole.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾為宮，是謂天統；

translations.literal: Yellow Bell as gong—this is called the heavenly succession;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell for gong—that is the heavenly succession;

sentences.zh: 林鍾為徵，是謂地統；

translations.literal: Forest Bell as zhi—this is called the earthly succession;
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell for zhi—that is the earthly succession;

sentences.zh: 太簇為商，是謂人統。

translations.literal: Great Cluster as shang—this is called the human succession.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster for shang—that is the human succession.

sentences.zh: 南呂為羽，於時屬秋；

translations.literal: Southern Lu as yu, in season belonging to autumn;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Lu for yu, belonging to autumn;

sentences.zh: 姑洗為角，於時屬春；

translations.literal: Maiden Wash as jiao, in season belonging to spring;
translations.idiomatic: Maiden Wash for jiao, belonging to spring;

sentences.zh: 應鍾為變宮，於時屬冬；

translations.literal: Responding Bell as altered gong, in season belonging to winter;
translations.idiomatic: Responding Bell as altered gong, belonging to winter;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓為變徵，於時屬夏。

translations.literal: Luxuriant Guest as altered zhi, in season belonging to summer.
translations.idiomatic: Luxuriant Guest as altered zhi, belonging to summer.

sentences.zh: 旋相為宮，而每律皆具七聲，而八十四調備焉。

translations.literal: Rotating each in turn as gong, every pitch pipe possesses all seven tones, and the eighty-four modes are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Each pipe in turn serves as gong; every pitch holds all seven tones, and eighty-four modes are made complete.

sentences.zh: 其圖八十四調以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the eighty-four modes is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart for the eighty-four modes.

sentences.zh: 自黃鍾至仲呂，則陽數極而為乾，故其位在左；

translations.literal: From Yellow Bell to Matured Lu, the yang numbers reach their limit and become Qian, therefore their position is on the left;
translations.idiomatic: From Yellow Bell to Matured Lu the yang count peaks in Qian, so these stand on the left;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓至應鍾，則陰數極而為坤，故其位在右。

translations.literal: From Luxuriant Guest to Responding Bell, the yin numbers reach their limit and become Kun, therefore their position is on the right.
translations.idiomatic: From Luxuriant Guest to Responding Bell the yin count peaks in Kun, so these stand on the right.

sentences.zh: 陰窮則歸本，故應鍾自生陰律；

translations.literal: When yin is exhausted it returns to the root, therefore Responding Bell itself generates the yin pitch pipes;
translations.idiomatic: When yin is spent it returns to origin, so Responding Bell itself begets the yin pipes;

sentences.zh: 陽窮則歸本，故仲呂自歸陽位。

translations.literal: when yang is exhausted it returns to the root, therefore Matured Lu itself returns to the yang position.
translations.idiomatic: when yang is spent it returns to origin, so Matured Lu itself reverts to the yang place.

sentences.zh: 律呂相生，起於《復》而成於《乾》，終始皆本於陽，故曰“樂由陽來”，六呂則同之而已。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes beget one another, beginning at "Return" and completing at "The Creative"; beginning and end both root in yang, hence it is said, "Music comes from yang"—the six yin pipes simply follow the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes generate one another from the hexagram "Return" to "The Creative"; start and finish both spring from yang, hence "music arises from yang"—the six yin pipes merely follow suit.

sentences.zh: 相生之位，分則為《乾》、《坤》之爻，合則為《既濟》、《未濟》之卦。

translations.literal: The positions of mutual generation, when divided become the lines of "The Creative" and "The Receptive"; when joined become the hexagrams "Already Fording" and "Not Yet Fording."
translations.idiomatic: The generating positions, split apart, are the lines of Qian and Kun; joined together, they form the hexagrams Already Fording and Not Yet Fording.

sentences.zh: 自黃鍾至仲呂為《既濟》，故屬陽而居左；

translations.literal: From Yellow Bell to Matured Lu is "Already Fording," therefore it belongs to yang and stands on the left;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell through Matured Lu is Already Fording, so it is yang and stands left;

sentences.zh: 自蕤賓至應鍾為《未濟》，故屬陰而居右。

translations.literal: From Luxuriant Guest to Responding Bell is "Not Yet Fording," therefore it belongs to yin and stands on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Luxuriant Guest through Responding Bell is Not Yet Fording, so it is yin and stands right.

sentences.zh: 《易》始於《乾》、《坤》而終於《既濟》、《未濟》，天地辨位而水火之氣交際於其中，造化之原皆自此出。

translations.literal: The "Changes" begins with "The Creative" and "The Receptive" and ends with "Already Fording" and "Not Yet Fording"; heaven and earth take their positions and the qi of water and fire meet within— the origin of creation all proceeds from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes opens with Qian and Kun and closes with Already Fording and Not Yet Fording; heaven and earth are set apart while water and fire mingle between—the wellspring of creation flows from here.

sentences.zh: 其圖十二律所生以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of what the twelve pitch pipes generate is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart of the twelve pipes' generation.

sentences.zh: 二十四氣差之毫厘，則或先天而太過，或後天而不及。

translations.literal: If the twenty-four qi are off by the smallest measure, then either they come ahead of heaven and exceed, or come behind heaven and fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Err by a hair in the twenty-four seasons and pitch may run ahead of heaven and overshoot, or lag behind and fall short.

sentences.zh: 在律為聲，在曆為氣。

translations.literal: In pitch pipes it is sound; in the calendar it is qi.
translations.idiomatic: Among pipes it is pitch; in the calendar it is breath.

sentences.zh: 若氣方得節，乃用中聲；

translations.literal: If qi has just reached the node, then use the central tone;
translations.idiomatic: When breath has only just reached a node, employ the central pitch;

sentences.zh: 氣已及中，猶用正律。

translations.literal: when qi has already reached the center, still use the correct pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: once breath has reached the midpoint, still use the orthodox pipes.

sentences.zh: 其圖十二律應二十四氣以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the twelve pitch pipes corresponding to the twenty-four qi is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart of the twelve pipes against the twenty-four qi.

sentences.zh: 漢津曰：“黃帝、夏禹之法，簡捷徑直，得於自然，故善作樂者以聲為本。

translations.literal: Wei Hanjin said: "The methods of the Yellow Emperor and Yu of Xia are simple, direct, and straight, obtained from nature; therefore those skilled in making music take sound as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hanjin said: "The Yellow Emperor and Yu of Xia worked by methods plain and direct, drawn from nature; hence the skilled composer takes pitch as root.

sentences.zh: 若得其聲，則形數、制度當自我出。

translations.literal: If one obtains the sound, then forms, numbers, and institutions should proceed from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Gain the pitch, and form, measure, and regulation will flow from you alone.

sentences.zh: 今以帝指為律，正聲之律十二，中聲之律十二，清聲凡四，共二十有八”雲。

translations.literal: Now taking the Emperor's finger-span as the pitch standard, there are twelve correct-tone pitch pipes, twelve central-tone pitch pipes, and four clear tones in all—twenty-eight altogether," he said.
translations.idiomatic: Today the sovereign's finger-width sets the standard: twelve orthodox pipes, twelve central pipes, and four clear tones—twenty-eight in all," he concluded.

sentences.zh: 其圖十二律鍾正聲以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the twelve pitch pipes, bells, and correct tones is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart of the twelve pipes, bells, and orthodox pitches.

sentences.zh: 堂上之樂，以人聲為貴，歌鍾居左，歌磬居右。

translations.literal: Hall music values the human voice above all; the song bells are placed on the left and the song chimes on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In hall music the human voice is paramount; song bells stand left, song chimes right.

sentences.zh: 近世之樂，曲不協律，歌不擇人，有先製譜而後命辭。

translations.literal: In recent-times music, songs do not accord with pitch, singers are not chosen for skill, and sometimes the score is made first and words assigned afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Modern music often mismatches melody and pitch, picks singers without care, and sometimes sets the score before the words.

sentences.zh: 奉常舊工，村野癃老者斥之。

translations.literal: Old musicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and decrepit village elders were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and withered old men from the countryside were turned away.

sentences.zh: 升歌之工，選擇惟艱，故堂上之樂鏗然特異焉。

translations.literal: Singers for the ascending song were chosen with utmost difficulty; therefore hall music rang out singular and distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending-song singers were chosen with exceptional rigor, so hall music resounded with a distinctive clarity.

sentences.zh: 其圖堂上樂以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of hall music is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart for hall music.

sentences.zh: 金玉之精，稟氣於乾，故堂上之樂，鍾必以金，磬必以玉。

translations.literal: The essences of metal and jade receive qi from Qian; therefore in hall music bells must be of metal and chimes must be of jade.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and jade distill breath from Qian; in hall music bells are cast of gold and chimes carved of jade.

sentences.zh: 《曆代樂儀》曰：“歌磬次歌鍾之西，以節登歌之句。

translations.literal: Records of Music Rituals through the Ages says: "The song chime comes next west of the song bell, to mark the phrases of the ascending song.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Rituals of Successive Ages records: "The song chime follows the song bell to the west, beating time for the ascending song.

sentences.zh: ”即《周官》頌磬也，神考肇造玉磬，聖上紹述先誌，而堂上之樂方備，非聖智兼全、金聲而玉振之者，安能與於天道哉？

translations.literal: " This is the praise chime of the Rites of Zhou; Shenzong first fashioned jade chimes, and the sage sovereign continued the prior design—only then was hall music complete. Without one whose sagely wisdom is fully united, whose metal sounds and jade resounds—how could one partake in the Way of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: This is the praise chime of the Zhou officers. Shenzong first created jade chimes; our sovereign carried forward that intent, and hall music at last stood complete. Only one in whom sagely wisdom is whole—whose metal sounds and jade answers—could share in Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 其圖金鍾玉磬以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of metal bells and jade chimes is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart for gold bells and jade stones.

sentences.zh: 《大晟》之製，天子親祀圓丘，則用景鍾為君圍，鎛鍾、特磬為臣圍，編鍾、編磬為民圍，非親祀則不用君圍。

translations.literal: Under the institutions of "Great Sheng," when the Son of Heaven personally sacrifices at the Round Mound, the Splendid Bell serves as the lord formation, great bells and single chimes as the minister formation, and sets of bells and chimes as the people formation; if it is not a personal sacrifice, the lord formation is not used.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Sheng system, when the emperor himself offers at the Round Mound, the Splendid Bell forms the lord circle, great bells and single chimes the minister circle, and serial bells and stones the people's circle—the lord circle is used only at personal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 漢津以謂：“宮架總攝四方之氣，故《大晟》之製，羽在上而以四方之禽，虡在下而以四方之獸，以象鳳儀、獸舞之狀。

translations.literal: Wei Hanjin held: "The palace stand governs the qi of the four directions; therefore in the "Great Sheng" institutions, yu is above with birds of the four directions, while the bell frames below bear beasts of the four directions, to represent the postures of the phoenix rite and beast dance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hanjin argued: "The palace stand gathers breath from the four quarters; in the Great Sheng design the yu pipes rise above with birds of each direction, while below the frames bear beasts of the four quarters, evoking phoenix ceremony and beast dance.

sentences.zh: 龍簨崇牙，製作華煥。

translations.literal: Dragon banners and elevated teeth—fashioned splendid and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon streamers and raised finials, wrought in splendid splendor.

sentences.zh: ”其圖宮架以此。

translations.literal: " The diagram of the palace stand is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the chart for the palace stand.

sentences.zh: 新樂肇興，法夏籥九成之數：文舞九成，終於垂衣拱手，無為而治；

translations.literal: With the new music's first rise, it followed the nine segments of the Xia yue flute: the civil dance in nine segments ended with draped robes, folded hands, and rule through nonaction;
translations.idiomatic: As the new music arose, it followed the Xia flute's ninefold measure: the civil dance's nine segments ended in robes flowing, hands folded, governance without exertion;

sentences.zh: 武舞九成，終於偃武修文，投戈講藝。

translations.literal: the martial dance in nine segments ended with laying down arms and cultivating culture, casting aside halberds to teach the arts.
translations.idiomatic: the martial dance's nine ended in sheathing arms for civil rule, casting spears aside to teach the arts.

sentences.zh: 每成進退疾徐，抑揚顧揖，皆各象方今之勳烈。

translations.literal: Each segment's advance and retreat, quickness and slowness, rising and falling, looking and bowing—all alike symbolized the present-day meritorious achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Each segment's advance and retreat, tempo and pause, rise and bow all mirrored the glorious deeds of the age.

sentences.zh: 文武八佾，左執籥，右秉翟。

translations.literal: The civil and martial eight rows: left hand holding the yue flute, right hand bearing pheasant feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight rows for civil and martial dance: flute in the left hand, pheasant plumes in the right.

sentences.zh: 蓋籥為聲之中，翟為文之華，秉中聲而昌文德。

translations.literal: For the yue is the center of sound, the feather is the glory of culture—bearing the central tone while flourishing civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The flute holds the middle of sound, the plume the bloom of culture—bearing central pitch to exalt civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 武舞八佾，執幹戈而進，以金鼓為節。

translations.literal: The martial dance's eight rows, advancing with shields and halberds, take metal and drum as beat.
translations.idiomatic: The martial eight rows advance with shield and spear, metal and drum marking time.

sentences.zh: 其圖二舞以此。

translations.literal: Its diagram of the two dances is based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the chart for the two dances.

sentences.zh: 又列八音之器，金部有七：曰景鍾，曰鎛鍾，曰編鍾，曰金錞，曰金鐲，曰金鐃，曰金鐸。

translations.literal: The instruments of the eight sounds were also listed; the metal category has seven: called Splendid Bell, great bell, set of bells, metal chun, metal wrist-rings, metal nao, and metal duo.
translations.idiomatic: The eight sounds were catalogued further: seven in the metal class—Splendid Bell, great bell, serial bells, metal chun, metal wrist-rings, metal cymbals, and metal clappers.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：

translations.literal: The explanation holds:
translations.idiomatic: The account runs thus:

sentences.zh: 景鍾乃樂之祖，而非常用之樂也。

translations.literal: The Splendid Bell is the ancestor of music, yet not music for ordinary use.
translations.idiomatic: The Splendid Bell is music's progenitor, not an instrument for daily performance.

sentences.zh: 黃帝五鍾，一曰景鍾。

translations.literal: Among the Yellow Emperor's five bells, one is called the Splendid Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Yellow Emperor's five bells, the first is the Splendid Bell.

sentences.zh: 景，大也。

translations.literal: Jing means great.
translations.idiomatic: Jing means "great."

sentences.zh: 鍾，四方之聲，以象厥成。

translations.literal: Zhong is the sound of the four directions, to symbolize their completion.
translations.idiomatic: The bell is the sound of the four quarters, imaging their fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 惟功大者其鍾大，世莫識其義久矣。

translations.literal: Only where merit is great is the bell great; the world has long failed to grasp this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Only great merit warrants a great bell—yet for ages none have understood this.

sentences.zh: 其聲則黃鍾之正，而律呂由是生焉。

translations.literal: Its sound is the orthodox Yellow Bell, and from it the pitch pipes are generated.
translations.idiomatic: Its pitch is orthodox Yellow Bell, and from it the pipes are born.

sentences.zh: 平時弗考，風至則鳴，鎛鍾形聲宏大，各司其辰，以管攝四方之氣。

translations.literal: In ordinary times it is not tested; when the wind comes it sounds. Great bells are vast in form and sound; each governs its double-hour, overseeing the qi of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: It is not sounded in daily use; when wind arrives it rings. Great bells are grand in shape and tone, each ruling its hour and gathering breath from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 編鍾隨月用律，雜比成文，聲韻清越。

translations.literal: Sets of bells follow the monthly pitch pipes, blended and patterned into composition, their sound bright and piercing.
translations.idiomatic: Serial bells follow the monthly pipes, woven into patterned phrases, their tone clear and ringing.

sentences.zh: 錞、鐲、鐃、鐸，古謂之四金。

translations.literal: Chun, zhuo, nao, and duo—in antiquity these were called the four metals.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, wrist-rings, cymbals, and clappers—the ancients named these the four metals.

sentences.zh: 鼓屬乎陽，金屬乎陰。

translations.literal: Drums belong to yang; metal belongs to yin.
translations.idiomatic: Drums appertain to yang; metal to yin.

sentences.zh: 陽造始而為之倡，故以金鎛和鼓陽動而不知已，故以金鐲節鼓。

translations.literal: Yang initiates and leads the way, therefore metal chun harmonize with drums; yang moves and does not know when to stop, therefore metal wrist-rings mark the drumbeats.
translations.idiomatic: Yang begins and leads, so metal chun answer the drum; yang acts without knowing rest, so metal wrist-rings set the drum's pace.

sentences.zh: 陽之用事，有時而終，故以金鐃止鼓。

translations.literal: When yang's work has its season and ends, metal nao stop the drums.
translations.idiomatic: When yang's task reaches its term, metal cymbals halt the drum.

sentences.zh: 時止則止，時行則行，天之道也，故以金鐸通鼓。

translations.literal: When the time stops, stop; when the time moves, move—this is heaven's way; therefore metal duo communicate with the drums.
translations.idiomatic: Stop when the season stops, move when it moves—that is Heaven's way; hence metal clappers signal the drum.

sentences.zh: 金乃《兌》音，《兌》為口舌，故金之屬皆象之。

translations.literal: Metal is the sound of "Joy"; "Joy" is the mouth and tongue, therefore all things of the metal category symbolize this.
translations.idiomatic: Metal is the pitch of Dui; Dui is mouth and tongue—hence every metal instrument images that.

sentences.zh: 石部有二：曰特磬，曰編磬。

translations.literal: The stone category has two: called the single chime and the set of chimes.
translations.idiomatic: The stone class has two: the single chime and the serial chimes.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：“依我磬聲”，以石有一定之聲，眾樂依焉，則鍾磬未嚐不相須也。

translations.literal: The explanation holds: "Obey my chime's sound"—because stone has a fixed sound upon which all music relies, bells and chimes have never been unneeded by each other.
translations.idiomatic: The account says: "Follow my chime's tone"—stone holds a fixed pitch on which all music depends; bells and chimes have never stood apart.

sentences.zh: 往者，國朝祀天地、宗廟及大朝會，宮架內止設鎛鍾，惟後廟乃用特磬，若已升祔後廟，遂置而不用。

translations.literal: Formerly, when our dynasty sacrificed to heaven and earth and the ancestral temple and at great court assemblies, within the palace stand only great bells were set up; only at the rear temple were single chimes used, and if one had already been enshrined in the rear temple, they were then set aside and not used.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier reigns, at sacrifices to heaven and earth, the ancestral shrines, and great court assemblies, the palace stand held only great bells; single chimes appeared only at the rear temple, and once a ruler was enshrined there, they were laid aside unused.

sentences.zh: 如此，則金石之聲小大不侔。

translations.literal: In this way the sounds of metal and stone, great and small, did not match.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the tones of metal and stone, large and small, were ill matched.

sentences.zh: 《大晟》之製，金石並用，以諧陰陽。

translations.literal: Under the institutions of "Great Sheng," metal and stone are both used to harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Sheng system, metal and stone are employed together to harmonize yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 漢津之法，以聲為主，必用泗濱之石，故《禹貢》必曰“浮磬”者，遠土而近於水，取之實難。

translations.literal: Wei Hanjin's method takes sound as primary and must use stone from the Si River bank; therefore the "Tribute of Yu" necessarily says "floating chimes"—distant territory yet near water, so obtaining it is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin's method puts pitch first and insists on stone from the Si River's bank; hence the Tribute of Yu speaks of "floating chimes"—far land, close water, and hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 昔奉常所用，乃以白石為之，其聲沉下，製作簡質，理宜改造焉。

translations.literal: What the Court of Imperial Sacrifices formerly used was made of white stone; its sound was low and sinking, and the workmanship was plain and simple—it was right that it be remade.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices had used white stone; the tone sank low and the craft was spare—remaking was plainly in order.

sentences.zh: 絲部有五：曰一弦琴，曰三弦琴，曰五弦琴，曰七弦琴，曰九弦琴，曰瑟。

translations.literal: The silk category has five: called the one-string zither, three-string zither, five-string zither, seven-string zither, nine-string zither, and the se.
translations.idiomatic: The silk class lists five types: the one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, and the se.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：漢津誦其師之說曰：“古者，聖人作五等之琴，琴主陽，一、三、五、七、九，生成之數也。

translations.literal: The explanation holds: Wei Hanjin recited his master's teaching, saying: "In antiquity the sages made zithers of five grades; the zither governs yang, and one, three, five, seven, and nine are numbers of generation.
translations.idiomatic: The account runs: Wei Hanjin quoted his teacher: "Ancient sages fashioned five grades of zither; the zither belongs to yang, and one, three, five, seven, and nine are generative numbers.

sentences.zh: 師延拊一弦之琴，昔人作三弦琴，蓋陽之數成於三。

translations.literal: Shi Yan played the one-string zither; men of old made the three-string zither, for the number of yang is completed in three.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yan strummed the one-string zither; ancients made the three-string zither because yang's count completes itself in three.

sentences.zh: 伏羲作琴有五弦，神農氏為琴七弦，琴書以九弦象九星。

translations.literal: Fuxi made the zither with five strings; Shennong made it seven strings; zither books take nine strings to symbolize the nine stars.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi gave the zither five strings; Shennong seven; zither lore sets nine strings to image the nine stars.

sentences.zh: 五等之琴，額長二寸四分，以象二十四氣；

translations.literal: For zithers of the five grades, the forehead is two inches and four tenths long, to symbolize the twenty-four qi;
translations.idiomatic: On the five grades of zither, the forehead measures two and four-tenths inches, imaging the twenty-four seasons;

sentences.zh: 嶽闊三分，以象三才；

translations.literal: the bridge is three tenths wide, to symbolize the Three Powers;
translations.idiomatic: the bridge spans three tenths, imaging the Three Powers;

sentences.zh: 嶽內取聲三尺六寸，以象期三百六十日：龍齗及折勢四分，以象四時：共長三尺九寸一分，成於三，極於九。

translations.literal: within the bridge the sounding length is three feet six inches, to symbolize the period of three hundred sixty days; the dragon's gums and the break in the curve are four tenths, to symbolize the four seasons: the total length is three feet nine inches and one tenth, completed in three and reaching the limit in nine.
translations.idiomatic: inside the bridge the sounding length is three feet six inches, imaging three hundred sixty days; the dragon's gums and the bent contour four tenths, imaging the four seasons—altogether three feet nine inches and one tenth, completing in three and peaking in nine.

sentences.zh: 九者，究也，復變而為一之義也。

translations.literal: Nine is exhaustion, the meaning of returning through change to become one again.
translations.idiomatic: Nine is completion—the sense of turning through change back into one.

sentences.zh: 《大晟》之瑟長七尺二寸，陰爻之數二十有四，極三才之陰數而七十有二，以象一歲之候。

translations.literal: The se of "Great Sheng" is seven feet two inches long; the number of yin lines is twenty-four, reaching the yin number of the Three Powers to seventy-two, to symbolize the markers of one year.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Sheng se measures seven feet two inches; twenty-four yin lines, summing the yin count of the Three Powers to seventy-two, image the seasons of a year.

sentences.zh: 既罷箏、築、阮，絲聲稍下，乃增瑟之數為六十有四，則八八之數法乎陰，琴之數則九十有九而法乎陽。

translations.literal: Once the zheng, zhu, and ruan were abolished and silk tones were somewhat lowered, the number of se was increased to sixty-four; then the number eight times eight follows yin, while the number of zithers is ninety-nine and follows yang.
translations.idiomatic: After the zheng, zhu, and ruan were retired and silk tones were lowered, the se were increased to sixty-four—the eight-by-eight count following yin—while zithers number ninety-nine and follow yang.

translations.literal: " (End of passage.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of passage.)

sentences.zh: 竹部有三：曰長笛，曰篪，曰簫。

translations.literal: The bamboo category has three: called the long flute, chi, and xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The bamboo class has three: the long flute, the chi, and the xiao.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：笛以一管而兼律呂，眾樂由焉。

translations.literal: The explanation holds: the flute with one tube encompasses both pitch pipes, and all music proceeds from it.
translations.idiomatic: The account runs: a single tube on the flute spans both yin and yang pipes—from it all music takes its course.

sentences.zh: 三竅成籥，三才之和寓焉。

translations.literal: Three apertures form the yue; the harmony of the Three Powers is embodied therein.
translations.idiomatic: Three holes make the yue—the concord of Heaven, Earth, and Man dwells within it.

sentences.zh: 六竅為笛，六律之聲備焉。

translations.literal: Six apertures make the flute; the sounds of the six pitch standards are complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: Six holes form the transverse flute, and the tones of the six pitch standards are fully present.

sentences.zh: 篪之製，采竹竅厚均者，用兩節，開六孔，以備十二律之聲，則篪之樂生於律。

translations.literal: In the making of the chi, one selects bamboo whose bore is evenly thick, uses two nodes, opens six holes to provide for the sounds of the twelve pitch pipes—then the music of the chi is born from pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The chi is fashioned from bamboo of even wall thickness and two nodes, pierced with six holes to supply the twelve pitch tones; thus chi music arises from the pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 樂始於律而成於簫。

translations.literal: Music begins with pitch pipes and is completed in the xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Music takes its start in the pitch pipes and finds completion in the xiao.

sentences.zh: 律準鳳鳴，以一管為一聲。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes are calibrated to the phoenix's call, with one tube for one tone.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch pipes take the phoenix's cry as their standard, one tube yielding one pitch.

sentences.zh: 簫集眾律，編而為器：參差其管，以象鳳翼，簫然清亮，以象鳳鳴。

translations.literal: The xiao gathers all pitch pipes and binds them into an instrument: the tubes are staggered to image the phoenix's wings; clear and bright like the xiao, it images the phoenix's cry.
translations.idiomatic: The xiao assembles the many pitch pipes into a single instrument, its tubes set at varying lengths to evoke phoenix wings—pure and ringing, evoking the phoenix's song.

sentences.zh: 匏部有六：曰竽笙，曰巢笙，曰和笙，曰閏餘匏，曰九星匏，曰七星匏。

translations.literal: The gourd category has six: called the yu sheng, nest sheng, harmony sheng, intercalary-surplus gourd, nine-star gourd, and seven-star gourd.
translations.idiomatic: The gourd class lists six types: the yu sheng, nest sheng, harmony sheng, intercalary-surplus gourd, nine-star gourd, and seven-star gourd.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：列其管為簫，聚其管為笙。

translations.literal: The explanation holds: array the tubes and it becomes a xiao; gather the tubes and it becomes a sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The account runs: spread the tubes apart and you have a xiao; cluster them together and you have a sheng.

sentences.zh: 鳳凰於飛，簫則象之；

translations.literal: When the phoenix takes flight, the xiao images it;
translations.idiomatic: When the phoenix soars, the xiao represents it;

sentences.zh: 鳳凰戾止，笙則象之。

translations.literal: when the phoenix alights and rests, the sheng images it.
translations.idiomatic: when the phoenix settles and perches, the sheng represents it.

sentences.zh: 故內皆用簧，皆施匏於下。

translations.literal: Therefore both use reeds within and both have gourds fitted below.
translations.idiomatic: Hence both employ reeds inside and mount gourds beneath.

sentences.zh: 前古以三十六簧為竽，十九簧為巢，十三簧為和，皆用十九數，而以管之長短、聲之大小為別。

translations.literal: In antiquity thirty-six reeds made the yu, nineteen reeds the nest, and thirteen reeds the harmony—all used the number nineteen, distinguished by the length of the tubes and the size of the sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient practice set thirty-six reeds for the yu, nineteen for the nest, and thirteen for the harmony—all keyed to the number nineteen, with tube length and pitch volume as the distinguishing marks.

sentences.zh: 八音之中，匏音廢絕久矣。

translations.literal: Among the eight tones, the gourd tone had long been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Of the eight categories of sound, the gourd voice had been extinct for ages.

sentences.zh: 後世以木代匏，乃更其製，下皆用匏，而並造十三簧者，以象閏餘。

translations.literal: Later ages replaced gourd with wood and altered the design: all had gourds below, while those with thirteen reeds together were made to image the intercalary surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations substituted wood for gourd and revised the form—all kept gourds at the base, while instruments built with thirteen reeds together symbolized the intercalary remainder.

sentences.zh: 十者，土之成數；

translations.literal: Ten is the completion number of earth;
translations.idiomatic: Ten is earth's number of completion;

sentences.zh: 三者，木之生數，木得土而能生也。

translations.literal: three is the generative number of wood, for wood receiving earth can generate.
translations.idiomatic: three is wood's generative number, since wood gains life through earth.

sentences.zh: 九簧者，以象九星。

translations.literal: The nine-reed type images the nine stars.
translations.idiomatic: The nine-reed instrument symbolizes the nine stars.

sentences.zh: 物得陽而生，九者，陽數之極也。

translations.literal: Things receiving yang are generated; nine is the utmost of yang numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Life comes through yang; nine is the yang number at its limit.

sentences.zh: 七簧者，以象七星。

translations.literal: The seven-reed type images the seven stars.
translations.idiomatic: The seven-reed instrument symbolizes the seven stars.

sentences.zh: 笙之形若鳥斂翼，鳥，火禽，火數七也。

translations.literal: The sheng's form is like a bird folding its wings; the bird is a fire creature, and seven is the number of fire.
translations.idiomatic: The sheng resembles a bird with folded wings; birds belong to fire, and fire's number is seven.

sentences.zh: 土部有一：曰塤。

translations.literal: The earth category has one: called the xun.
translations.idiomatic: The earth class has one instrument: the xun.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：釋《詩》者以塤、篪異器而同聲，然八音孰不同聲，必以塤、篪為況？

translations.literal: The explanation holds: commentators on the Odes take the xun and chi as different instruments yet of the same sound—but which of the eight tones does not differ in sound? Why must the xun and chi be singled out as examples?
translations.idiomatic: The account runs: Odes commentators cite the xun and chi as distinct vessels sharing one tone—yet which of the eight tones does not share tones? Why hold up xun and chi alone?

sentences.zh: 嚐博詢其旨，蓋八音取聲相同者，惟塤、篪為然。

translations.literal: Once inquiry was broadly made into its purport, it appears that among the eight tones only the xun and chi truly take the same sound.
translations.idiomatic: On broad inquiry into the matter, only the xun and chi among the eight tones genuinely share identical pitch.

sentences.zh: 塤、篪皆六孔而以五竅取聲。

translations.literal: The xun and chi both have six holes yet take their sound from five apertures.
translations.idiomatic: Both xun and chi have six holes but produce pitch through five openings.

sentences.zh: 十二律始於黃鍾，終於應鍾。

translations.literal: The twelve pitch pipes begin with Yellow Bell and end with Responding Bell.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve standard pipes run from Yellow Bell to Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 二者，其竅盡合則為黃鍾，其竅盡開則為應鍾，餘樂不然。

translations.literal: For these two, when all apertures are closed the tone is Yellow Bell; when all are open the tone is Responding Bell—other instruments are not so.
translations.idiomatic: With these two alone, every hole closed yields Yellow Bell and every hole open yields Responding Bell; no other instrument behaves this way.

sentences.zh: 故惟塤、篪相應。

translations.literal: Therefore only the xun and chi correspond to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Hence only the xun and chi answer one another.

sentences.zh: 革部十有二：曰晉鼓，曰建鼓，曰鞀鼓，曰雷鼓，曰雷鞀，曰靈鼓，曰路鞀，曰路鼓，曰路鞀，曰雅鼓，曰相鼓，曰搏拊。

translations.literal: The leather category has twelve: called the Jin drum, mounted drum, tao drum, thunder drum, thunder tao, spirit drum, road tao, road drum, road tao, ya drum, xiang drum, and bofu.
translations.idiomatic: The leather class lists twelve: the Jin drum, mounted drum, tao drum, thunder drum, thunder tao, spirit drum, road tao, road drum, road tao, ya drum, xiang drum, and bofu.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：凡言樂者，必曰鍾鼓，蓋鍾為秋分之音而屬陰，鼓為春分之音而屬陽。

translations.literal: The explanation holds: whenever one speaks of music one necessarily says bells and drums—for the bell is the tone of the autumn equinox and belongs to yin, while the drum is the tone of the spring equinox and belongs to yang.
translations.idiomatic: The account runs: music is always spoken of as bells and drums—the bell belongs to the autumn equinox and yin, the drum to the spring equinox and yang.

sentences.zh: 金奏待鼓而後進者，雷發聲而後群物皆鳴也；

translations.literal: That metal performance waits for the drum before advancing images thunder sounding forth and then all things giving voice;
translations.idiomatic: Metal music waits upon the drum before proceeding, as thunder breaks and every creature answers with sound;

sentences.zh: 鼓復用金以節樂者，雷收聲而後蟄蟲坯戶也。

translations.literal: that the drum in turn uses metal to mark the music images thunder withdrawing its sound and then hibernating insects sealing their doors.
translations.idiomatic: and the drum then employs metal to regulate the music, as thunder falls silent and dormant insects close their burrows.

sentences.zh: 《周官》以晉鼓鼓金奏，陽為陰唱也。

translations.literal: The "Offices of Zhou" uses the Jin drum to beat for metal performance—yang singing for yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou has the Jin drum strike for metal music—yang voicing for yin.

sentences.zh: 建鼓，少昊氏所造，以節眾樂。

translations.literal: The mounted drum was made by Shaohao, to mark the rhythm of all music.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao invented the mounted drum to keep time for the full ensemble.

sentences.zh: 夏加四足，謂之足鼓；

translations.literal: The Xia added four feet, calling it the foot drum;
translations.idiomatic: Under Xia four legs were added, making the foot drum;

sentences.zh: 商貫之以柱，謂之楹鼓；

translations.literal: the Shang ran a pillar through it, calling it the pillar drum;
translations.idiomatic: Shang drove a pillar through it, making the pillar drum;

sentences.zh: 周縣而擊之，謂之縣鼓。

translations.literal: the Zhou suspended it and struck it, calling it the suspended drum.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou hung it up to be struck, making the suspended drum.

sentences.zh: 鞀者，鼓之兆也。

translations.literal: The tao is the precursor of the drum.
translations.idiomatic: The tao is the drum's herald.

sentences.zh: 天子錫諸侯樂，以將之；

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven bestowed music upon feudal lords, he used the mounted drum to lead it;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor granted music to feudal lords, a mounted drum led the procession;

sentences.zh: 賜伯、子、男樂，以鞀將之。

translations.literal: to earls, viscounts, and barons he granted music led by the tao.
translations.idiomatic: for earls, viscounts, and barons the gift was music led by the tao.

sentences.zh: 先眾樂，鞀則先鼓而已。

translations.literal: Before the full ensemble, the tao merely beats first.
translations.idiomatic: Ahead of the whole orchestra, the tao simply strikes first.

sentences.zh: 以雷鼓鼓天神，因天聲以祀天也；

translations.literal: The thunder drum beats for the worship of the heavenly spirit, taking heaven's sound to sacrifice to heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The thunder drum serves heaven's spirit, using heaven's voice in sacrifice to heaven;

sentences.zh: 以靈鼓鼓社祭，以天為神，則地為靈也；

translations.literal: the spirit drum beats for the community altar sacrifice—heaven taken as the spirit, then earth is the numen;
translations.idiomatic: the spirit drum serves the earth altar—where heaven is spirit, earth is the numinous power;

sentences.zh: 以路鼓鼓鬼享，人道之大也。

translations.literal: the road drum beats for the ghost offering—the greatest of human ways.
translations.idiomatic: the road drum serves offerings to the dead—the highest expression of human rite.

sentences.zh: 以舞者迅疾，以雅節之，故曰雅鼓。

translations.literal: Because dancers move swiftly, the ya drum marks their rhythm; hence it is called the ya drum.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers move with quick steps, and the ya drum sets their pace—hence its name.

sentences.zh: 相所以輔相於樂，今用節舞者之步，故曰相鼓。

translations.literal: The xiang assists and complements the music; today it is used to mark the dancers' steps—hence it is called the xiang drum.
translations.idiomatic: The xiang supports the ensemble; now it keeps the dancers' footfall—hence the xiang drum.

sentences.zh: 登歌今奏擊拊，以革為之，實之以糠，升歌之鼓節也。

translations.literal: For the ascending song performance today, the bofu is struck; made of leather and filled with chaff, it is the drum-beat for the ascending song.
translations.idiomatic: In present ascending-song rites the bofu is played—a leather frame stuffed with chaff, beating time for the raised hymn.

sentences.zh: 木部有二：曰，曰。

translations.literal: The wood category has two: called the Zhu and the Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The wood class has two instruments: the zhu and the yu.

sentences.zh: 其說以謂：之作樂。
