translations.literal: The explanation holds: the Zhu begins music.
translations.idiomatic: The account runs: the zhu begins the music.

sentences.zh: 之止樂，漢津嚐問於李良，良曰：“聖人製作之旨，皆在《易》中。

translations.literal: The Yu ends music; Hanjin once asked Li Liang, and Liang said: "The sages' intent in making these instruments is all contained in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: The yu ends the music. Wei Hanjin once questioned Li Liang, who replied: "The purpose of the sages' craftsmanship lies entirely in the Changes.

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 'Zhen—to initiate.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes reads: 'Zhen means to begin.

sentences.zh: 《艮》，止也。

translations.literal: Gen—to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Gen means to stop.

sentences.zh: ’、之義，如斯而已。

translations.literal: ' The meaning of the Zhu and the Yu is simply this.
translations.idiomatic: ' So much for the meaning of the zhu and the yu.

sentences.zh: 以木為底，下實而上虛。

translations.literal: With wood as the base, solid below and hollow above.
translations.idiomatic: Wood forms the base, solid at the bottom and hollow on top.

sentences.zh: 《震》一陽在二陰之下，象其卦之形也。

translations.literal: Zhen has one yang below two yin, imaging the form of its hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen places one yang beneath two yin, mirroring the hexagram's shape.

sentences.zh: 擊其中，聲出虛，為眾樂倡。

translations.literal: Strike its center and sound issues from the hollow—it leads all music.
translations.idiomatic: Struck at the center, sound rises from the void, and it leads the whole orchestra.

sentences.zh: 《震》為雷，雷出地奮，為春分之音，故為眾樂之倡，而外飾以山林物生之狀。

translations.literal: Zhen is thunder; thunder bursts from the earth—the tone of the spring equinox—therefore it leads all music, while outwardly it is adorned with the forms of mountain forests and growing things.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen stands for thunder, thunder leaping from the earth—the spring-equinox tone—so it leads all music, its exterior decorated with images of woodland growth.

sentences.zh: 《艮》位寅，為虎，虎伏則以象止樂。

translations.literal: Gen occupies the yin position and is the tiger; when the tiger crouches it images stopping the music.
translations.idiomatic: Gen sits at yin and is the tiger; the crouching tiger images the music's end.

sentences.zh: 背有二十七刻，三九陽數之窮。

translations.literal: On its back are twenty-seven notches—three times nine, the exhaustion of yang numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Its back bears twenty-seven marks—three nines, yang's number spent.

sentences.zh: 戛之以竹，裂而為十，古或用十寸，或裂而為十二，陰數。

translations.literal: It is tapped with bamboo, split into ten; in antiquity some used ten inches, or split it into twelve—a yin number.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo strikes it, split into ten segments; ancients sometimes used ten inches, or divided it into twelve—a yin count.

sentences.zh: 十二者，二六之數，陽窮而以陰止之。

translations.literal: Twelve is the number two times six—yang exhausted and stopped by yin.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve is twice six: yang spent, yin brings halt.

sentences.zh: 又有度、量、權、衡四法，候氣、運律、教樂、運譜四議，與律曆、運氣或相表裏，甚精微矣，茲獨采其言樂事顯明者。

translations.literal: There were also the four methods of measure, capacity, weight, and balance, and the four deliberations on awaiting qi, operating pitch pipes, teaching music, and operating notation—matters sometimes inner and outer to pitch calendrics and circulating qi, exceedingly subtle; here only those statements on music that are clear and explicit are selected.
translations.idiomatic: The work also treated measures, capacity, weights, and balances, and deliberations on awaiting qi, tuning pipes, teaching music, and managing notation—topics intertwined with calendrics and circulating qi, and exceedingly refined; only the passages on music that speak plainly are excerpted here.

sentences.zh: 幾為書二十卷。

translations.literal: The book came to nearly twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation ran to nearly twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 說者以謂蔡京使昺為緣飾之，以布告天下雲。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Cai Jing had Bing embellish it to proclaim it to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Cai Jing had Bing adorn the text to broadcast it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，賜貢士聞喜宴於辟雍，仍用雅樂，罷瓊林苑宴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, the Court Graduate Celebration Banquet was granted at the Imperial Academy, still using court music, and the Qionglin Garden banquet was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 the Wenxi banquet for new graduates was held at the Imperial Academy with court music, and the Qionglin Garden feast was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎劉煥言：“州郡歲貢士，例有宴設，名曰‘鹿鳴’，乞於斯時許用雅樂，易去倡優淫哇之聲。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Liu Huan said: "Each year the prefectures present graduates and customarily hold a banquet called the 'Deer Call'; I beg that at that time court music be permitted and the sounds of entertainers and vulgar tunes be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan, Vice Minister of War, memorialized: "Prefectures yearly banquet their presented scholars in the 'Deer Call' feast; I ask that court music be allowed on that occasion and the voices of actors and licentious airs be banished.

sentences.zh: ”八月，太常言：“宗廟、太社、太稷並為大祠，今太社、太稷登歌而不設宮架樂舞，獨為未備，請迎神、送神、詣罍洗、歸復位、奉俎、退文舞、迎武舞、亞終獻、望燎樂曲，並用宮架樂，設於北墉之北。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "The ancestral temple, Grand Altar of Soil, and Grand Altar of Grain are all great sacrifices; now at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain there is ascending song but no palace-stand music and dance—this alone is incomplete. We request that the music for welcoming the spirit, escorting the spirit, proceeding to the libation ewer, returning to position, presenting the offering, withdrawing the civil dance, welcoming the martial dance, the second and final offerings, and the fire-gazing rites all employ palace-stand music, set north of the northern wall.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "The ancestral temple, Grand Altar of Soil, and Grand Altar of Grain are all major rites; yet at the soil and grain altars ascending song is performed without palace-stand music and dance—an omission alone. We ask that music for spirit-welcoming, spirit-escort, libation, return to station, offering presentation, civil-dance withdrawal, martial-dance entry, secondary and final offerings, and fire-gazing all use palace-stand music placed north of the outer north wall.

sentences.zh: ”詔皆從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Edicts approved every item.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，議禮局上親祠登歌之製

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, the Rites Deliberation Bureau submitted the arrangement for ascending song at the emperor's personal sacrifice
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year three the Rites Deliberation Bureau presented the layout for ascending song at the emperor's own sacrifice

translations.idiomatic: One metal bell, placed to the east;

translations.literal: one jade chime, in the west: both facing north.
translations.idiomatic: one jade chime, placed to the west—both facing north.

translations.literal: One zhu, north of the metal bell, slightly west;
translations.idiomatic: One zhu, north of the metal bell, a little to the west;

sentences.zh: 一，在玉磬北，稍東。

translations.literal: One yu, north of the jade chime, slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: One yu, north of the jade chime, a little to the east.

sentences.zh: 搏拊二：一在北，一在北，東西相向。

translations.literal: Two bofu: one north of the zhu, one north of the yu, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two bofu: one north of the zhu and one north of the yu, set east and west and facing each other.

sentences.zh: 一弦、三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴各一，瑟四，在金鍾之南，西上；

translations.literal: One each of the one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, and four se, south of the metal bell, ascending to the west;
translations.idiomatic: One each of the one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, plus four se, south of the metal bell, ranked westward;

sentences.zh: 玉磬之南亦如之，東上。

translations.literal: south of the jade chime the same arrangement, ascending to the east.
translations.idiomatic: south of the jade chime the same, ranked eastward.

translations.idiomatic: Also to the east of the noon steps

translations.idiomatic: One intercalary-surplus gourd and one xiao, each placed south of the nest sheng.

translations.idiomatic: Also to the west of the noon steps

translations.idiomatic: at the ancestral temple, west of the Grand Steps; at the imperial ancestral rite, east of the west steps; at a grand court assembly, west of the censer table on the red courtyard)

translations.idiomatic: , place two flutes, one chi, two nest sheng, and two harmony sheng in a single row, ranked eastward.

translations.literal: One xun, south of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: One xun, south of the flute.

translations.idiomatic: One seven-star gourd and one nine-star gourd, placed south of the nest sheng.

sentences.zh: 簫一，在九星匏西。

translations.literal: One xiao, west of the nine-star gourd.
translations.idiomatic: One xiao, west of the nine-star gourd.

sentences.zh: 鍾、磬、敔、博拊、琴、瑟工各坐於壇上

translations.literal: The bell, chime, yu, bofu, zither, and se players each sit on the altar platform
translations.idiomatic: Players of bell, chime, yu, bofu, zither, and se each sit upon the altar

translations.literal: Two Masters of Music south of the bells and chimes; four singers east of the yu—all facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two music masters south of the bells and chime-stones; four lead singers east of the yu, all arrayed to face one another east and west.

translations.idiomatic: One commander bearing the banner and regalia, posted west of the music frame and facing east.

translations.literal: for the Bright Hall, Ancestral Temple, and branch temples, on the hall floor; for temple shrines, on the hall platform)
translations.idiomatic: at the Bright Hall, Ancestral Temple, and branch temples, upon the hall floor; at temple shrines, upon the hall platform)

translations.idiomatic: at the Ancestral Temple and branch temples, to either side of the Grand Steps; at the Bright Hall and temple shrines, between the upper and lower flights; if no palace stand was used, all ascent-music players sat)

translations.literal: Two Masters of Music south of the bells and chimes; four singers to the east—all facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two music masters south of the bells and chime-stones; four lead singers to the east, all arrayed to face one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 執麾挾仗色掌事一名，在樂虡之西，東向。

translations.literal: One banner-bearer and color-attendant steward, west of the music stand, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One commander bearing the banner and regalia, posted west of the music frame and facing east.

sentences.zh: 樂正公服，執麾挾仗色掌事平巾幘，樂工黑介幘，並緋繡鸞衫、白絹抹帶

translations.idiomatic: Music masters wore court robes; the banner commander wore a plain zez cap; musicians wore black zez caps—all in scarlet phoenix-embroidered jackets with white silk waist sashes

translations.idiomatic: at the three capitals, military commission seats, and the like, in annual rites to the altars of soil and grain, the wind, rain, and thunder spirits, and the Confucian offering to the Cultural King, ascent music was used with the same instrument layout as for yearly major and medium-sacrifice ascent music)

sentences.zh: 又上太祠宮架、二舞之製：

translations.literal: They also submitted the arrangement for palace-stand music and the two dances at major sacrifices:
translations.idiomatic: The bureau next presented the palace-stand music and two-dance protocol for major sacrifices:

sentences.zh: 四方各設鎛鍾三，各依月律。

translations.literal: On each of the four sides were set three bofu bells, each according to its monthly pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Each cardinal side received three bofu bells, tuned to the monthly pitches.

sentences.zh: 編鍾一，編磬一。

translations.literal: One serial bell set and one serial chime set.
translations.idiomatic: One rank of serial bells and one of serial chimes.

sentences.zh: 北方，應鍾起西，編鍾次之，黃鍾次之，編磬次之，大呂次之，皆北向。

translations.literal: On the north, Yingzhong began in the west, then the serial bells, then Huangzhong, then the serial chimes, then Dalü—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Northward: Yingzhong began in the west, followed by serial bells, Huangzhong, serial chimes, and Dalü—all facing north.

sentences.zh: 東方，太簇起北，編鍾次之，夾鍾次之，編磬次之，姑洗次之，皆東向。

translations.literal: On the east, Taicu began in the north, then the serial bells, then Jiazhong, then the serial chimes, then Guxian—all facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward: Taicu began in the north, followed by serial bells, Jiazhong, serial chimes, and Guxian—all facing east.

sentences.zh: 南方，仲呂起東，編鍾次之，蕤賓次之，編磬次之，林鍾次之，皆北向。

translations.literal: On the south, Zhonglü began in the east, then the serial bells, then Ruibin, then the serial chimes, then Linzhong—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Southward: Zhonglü began in the east, followed by serial bells, Ruibin, serial chimes, and Linzhong—all facing north.

sentences.zh: 西方，夷則起南，編鍾次之，南呂次之，編磬次之，無射次之，皆西向。

translations.literal: On the west, Yize began in the south, then the serial bells, then Nanlü, then the serial chimes, then Wushe—all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Westward: Yize began in the south, followed by serial bells, Nanlü, serial chimes, and Wushe—all facing west.

sentences.zh: 設十二特磬，各在鎛鍾之內。

translations.literal: Twelve individual chimes were set, each within its bofu bell.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve individual chime-stones were placed, each within its bofu bell.

sentences.zh: 植建鼓、鞞鼓、應鼓於四隅。

translations.literal: Foundation drums, side drums, and answering drums were planted at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: Foundation, side, and answering drums stood at the four corners.

sentences.zh: 設、於北架內，在左，在右。

translations.literal: Zhu and yu were set within the northern frame: the zhu on the left, the yu on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Within the northern frame stood the zhu and yu: the zhu to the left, the yu to the right.

sentences.zh: 雷鼓、雷鞀各二

translations.literal: Two thunder drums and two thunder rattles each
translations.idiomatic: Two thunder drums and two thunder rattles each

sentences.zh: （地祇以靈鼓，靈鞀，太廟、別廟以路鼓、路鞀）〉

translations.literal: for Earth Spirits, spirit drums and spirit rattles; for the Ancestral Temple and branch temples, road drums and road rattles)
translations.idiomatic: for rites to Earth Spirits, spirit drums and spirit rattles; for the Ancestral Temple and branch temples, road drums and road rattles)

sentences.zh: 分東西，在歌工之側。

translations.literal: They were divided east and west, beside the singers.
translations.idiomatic: They stood east and west, flanking the singers.

sentences.zh: 瑟二，在東。

translations.literal: Two se, in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Two se, placed to the east.

sentences.zh: 次，一弦、三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴各二，各為一列。

translations.literal: Next, two each of the one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, each forming one row.
translations.idiomatic: Next came two each of the one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, each in its own row.

sentences.zh: 西亦如之。

translations.literal: The west was arranged the same way.
translations.idiomatic: The west side mirrored this.

sentences.zh: 巢笙、簫、竽、篪、塤、笛各四，為四列，在雷鼓之後

translations.literal: Four each of nest sheng, xiao, yu sheng, chi, xun, and flute, forming four rows, behind the thunder drums
translations.idiomatic: Four each of nest sheng, xiao, yu sheng, chi, xun, and flute in four rows, behind the thunder drums

sentences.zh: （若地祇即在靈鼓後，太廟、別廟在路鼓後）〉

translations.literal: for Earth Spirits they stood behind the spirit drums; for the Ancestral Temple and branch temples, behind the road drums)
translations.idiomatic: for Earth Spirits, behind the spirit drums; for the Ancestral Temple and branch temples, behind the road drums)

sentences.zh: 晉鼓一，在笛之後：俱北向。

translations.literal: One Jin drum, behind the flutes: all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: One Jin drum behind the flutes—all facing north.

sentences.zh: 副樂正二人在、之北。

translations.literal: Two deputy Masters of Music north of the zhu and yu.
translations.idiomatic: Two deputy music masters north of the zhu and yu.

sentences.zh: 歌工八人，左右各四，在、之南，東西相向。

translations.literal: Eight singers, four on each side, south of the zhu and yu, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Eight lead singers—four to each side—south of the zhu and yu, arrayed to face one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 執麾挾仗色掌事一名，在宮架西，北向。

translations.literal: One banner-bearer and color-attendant steward, west of the palace stand, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: One banner commander west of the palace stand, facing north.

sentences.zh: 副樂正本色公服，執麾挾仗色掌事及樂正平巾幘，服同登歌樂工

translations.literal: Deputy Masters of Music wore their regular official robes; the banner-bearer and color-attendant steward and the Master of Music wore plain-cloth zez, with dress the same as ascent-music workers
translations.idiomatic: Deputy music masters wore their regular court robes; the banner commander and music masters wore plain zez caps, dressed like ascent-music musicians

sentences.zh: （凡軒架之樂三面，其製，宮架之南機；

translations.literal: elevated-stand music on three sides; its arrangement follows the southern frame of the palace stand;
translations.idiomatic: For elevated-stand music on three sides, the layout follows the palace stand's southern frame;

sentences.zh: 判架之樂二面，其製，又去軒架之北面；

translations.literal: half-stand music on two sides; its arrangement likewise omits the north side of the elevated stand;
translations.idiomatic: Half-stand music on two sides drops the north wing of the elevated stand;

sentences.zh: 特架之樂一面）〉

translations.literal: special-stand music on one side)
translations.idiomatic: special-stand music on a single side)

sentences.zh: 文武二舞並同親祠，惟二舞郎並紫平冕、皂繡袍、銀褐裙、白絹抹帶，與親祠稍異。

translations.literal: The civil and martial dances were the same as at the personal sacrifice, except that dance officers all wore purple flat crowns, black embroidered robes, silver-brown skirts, and white silk sash bands—slightly different from the personal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and martial dance followed the personal-sacrifice protocol, but dance officers wore purple flat crowns, black embroidered robes, silver-brown skirts, and white silk waist sashes—a slight variation from the personal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔並頒行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all of this promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that all these regulations be issued.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝御崇政殿，親按宴樂，召侍從以上侍立。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Emperor presided at Chongzheng Hall, personally rehearsing banquet music, and summoned attendants-in-ordinary and above to stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Emperor went to Chongzheng Hall, personally rehearsed the banquet music, and had all court attendants from Attendant-in-Ordinary upward stand by.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“《大晟之樂》已薦之郊廟，而未施於宴饗。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The music of the Great Sheng has already been offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, but has not yet been applied to banquets and feasts.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The Great Sheng music has already been presented at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, yet it has not been extended to banquets and feasts.

sentences.zh: 比詔有司，以《大晟》樂播之教坊，試於殿庭，五聲既具，無惉懘焦急之聲，嘉與天下共之，可以所進樂頒之天下，其舊樂悉禁。

translations.literal: Recently We ordered the responsible offices to broadcast the Great Sheng music through the Music Office and test it in the palace courtyard; the five tones are now complete, with no discordant or harsh sounds. We rejoice to share this with all under Heaven. The submitted music may be issued throughout the realm, and all old music is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Recently We ordered the responsible offices to broadcast the Great Sheng music through the Music Office and test it in the palace courtyard. The five tones are now complete, without discord or harshness. We rejoice to share this with the world. Let the submitted music be issued throughout the realm, and let all old music be forbidden.

sentences.zh: ”於是令尚書省立法，新徵、角二調曲譜已經按試者，並令大晟府刊行，後續有譜，依此。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat was ordered to establish law: newly tested score-registers for the zhi and jiao modes were all to be published by the Great Sheng Prefecture, and any later scores were to follow this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was then ordered to codify the rule: newly tested score-registers for the zhi and jiao modes were to be published by the Great Sheng Prefecture, with later scores to follow the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 其宮、商、羽調曲譜自從舊，新樂器五聲、八音方全。

translations.literal: Score-registers for the gong, shang, and yu modes continued under the old practice; the new instruments now completed the five tones and eight categories of sound.
translations.idiomatic: Registers for the gong, shang, and yu modes remained under the old practice; with the new instruments, the five tones and eight sound categories were now complete.

sentences.zh: 塤、篪、匏、笙、石磬之類已經按試者，大晟府畫圖疏說頒行，教坊、鈞容直、開封府各頒降二副。

translations.literal: For xun, chi, gourd, sheng, stone chimes, and the like that had already been tested, the Great Sheng Prefecture was to publish illustrated explanations; the Music Office, the Palace Guard Music Corps, and Kaifeng Prefecture each received two copies.
translations.idiomatic: For xun, chi, gourd, sheng, stone chimes, and the like already tested, the Great Sheng Prefecture was to issue illustrated explanations; the Music Office, Palace Guard Music Corps, and Kaifeng Prefecture each received two sets.

sentences.zh: 開封府用所頒樂器，明示依式造粥，教坊、鈞容直及中外不得違。

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefecture was to use the issued instruments and clearly require manufacture according to the prescribed pattern; the Music Office, Palace Guard Music Corps, and all within and beyond the court were not to deviate.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefecture was to use the issued instruments and require manufacture strictly according to the prescribed specifications; the Music Office, Palace Guard Music Corps, and all within and beyond the court were forbidden to deviate.

sentences.zh: 今輒高下其聲，或別為他聲，或移改增損樂器，舊來淫哇之聲，如打斷、哨笛、呀鼓、十般舞、小鼓腔、小笛之類與其曲名，悉行禁止，違者與聽者悉坐罪。

translations.literal: Henceforth anyone who arbitrarily raised or lowered pitches, altered them into other sounds, or moved, added to, or reduced instruments, together with the old licentious sounds—such as daduan, whistle-flute, ya-drum, tenfold dance, small-drum cavity, small-flute, and the like, along with their tune titles—was wholly forbidden; violators and listeners alike would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who arbitrarily altered pitch, substituted other tones, or rearranged, added to, or reduced instruments, together with the old licentious repertoire—daduan, whistle-flute, ya-drum, tenfold dance, small-drum cavity, small-flute, and the like, with their tune titles—was wholly forbidden; violators and listeners alike would be punished.

sentences.zh: 八月，大晟府奏，以雅樂中聲播於宴樂，舊闕徵、角二調，及無土、石、匏三音，今樂並已增入。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Great Sheng Prefecture memorialized: the middle tones of ceremonial music were to be broadcast in banquet music; formerly missing were the zhi and jiao modes, and the earth, stone, and gourd categories of sound—now all had been added to the music.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Great Sheng Prefecture reported that the central tones of ceremonial music would be extended to banquet music. The zhi and jiao modes had long been absent, as had the earth, stone, and gourd voices of the eight sounds; all were now incorporated into the new repertoire.

sentences.zh: 詔頒降天下。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it issued throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that it be promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔：“《大晟樂》頒於太學、辟雍，諸生習學，所服冠以弁，袍以素紗、皂緣，紳帶，佩玉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict: "The Great Sheng music is to be issued to the Imperial Academy and Imperial College; students shall study it; the headwear they shall wear is the bian cap; robes of plain gauze with black trim, sash belt, and jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict declared: "The Great Sheng music shall be distributed to the Imperial Academy and Imperial College for student instruction. Students shall wear the bian cap, robes of plain gauze with black edging, sash belts, and jade pendants."

sentences.zh: ”從劉昺製也。

translations.literal: "—following regulations devised by Liu Bing.
translations.idiomatic: "—following regulations devised by Liu Bing.

sentences.zh: 昺又上言曰：“五行之氣，有生有克，四時之禁，不可不頒示天下。

translations.literal: Bing further submitted: "The qi of the Five Phases has generation and restraint; the seasonal prohibitions cannot fail to be promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Bing further memorialized: "The qi of the Five Phases both generates and restrains; the seasonal prohibitions on music cannot go unannounced to the realm."

sentences.zh: 盛德在木，角聲乃作，得羽而生，以徵為相；

translations.literal: When flourishing virtue resides in Wood, the jiao tone is produced; it receives life from yu and takes zhi as its minister;
translations.idiomatic: When flourishing virtue rests in Wood, the jiao tone arises; it draws life from yu and takes zhi as its ally;

sentences.zh: 若用商則刑，用宮則戰，故春禁宮、商。

translations.literal: if shang is used there will be punishments, if gong is used there will be warfare—hence in spring gong and shang are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: if shang is employed punishments follow, if gong is employed warfare follows—therefore in spring gong and shang are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 盛德在火，徵聲乃作，得角而生，以宮為相；

translations.literal: When flourishing virtue resides in Fire, the zhi tone is produced; it receives life from jiao and takes gong as its minister;
translations.idiomatic: When flourishing virtue rests in Fire, the zhi tone arises; it draws life from jiao and takes gong as its ally;

sentences.zh: 若用羽則刑，用商則戰，故夏禁商、羽。

translations.literal: if yu is used there will be punishments, if shang is used there will be warfare—hence in summer shang and yu are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: if yu is employed punishments follow, if shang is employed warfare follows—therefore in summer shang and yu are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 盛德在土，宮聲乃作，得徵而生，以商為相；

translations.literal: When flourishing virtue resides in Earth, the gong tone is produced; it receives life from zhi and takes shang as its minister;
translations.idiomatic: When flourishing virtue rests in Earth, the gong tone arises; it draws life from zhi and takes shang as its ally;

sentences.zh: 若用角則刑，用羽則戰，故季夏土王，宜禁角、羽。

translations.literal: if jiao is used there will be punishments, if yu is used there will be warfare—hence in late summer when Earth is sovereign, jiao and yu should be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: if jiao is employed punishments follow, if yu is employed warfare follows—therefore in late summer, when Earth holds sway, jiao and yu should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 盛德在金，商聲乃作，得宮而生，以羽為相；

translations.literal: When flourishing virtue resides in Metal, the shang tone is produced; it receives life from gong and takes yu as its minister;
translations.idiomatic: When flourishing virtue rests in Metal, the shang tone arises; it draws life from gong and takes yu as its ally;

sentences.zh: 若用徵則刑，用角則戰，故秋禁徵、角。

translations.literal: if zhi is used there will be punishments, if jiao is used there will be warfare—hence in autumn zhi and jiao are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: if zhi is employed punishments follow, if jiao is employed warfare follows—therefore in autumn zhi and jiao are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 盛德在水，羽聲乃作，得商而生，以角為相；

translations.literal: When flourishing virtue resides in Water, the yu tone is produced; it receives life from shang and takes jiao as its minister;
translations.idiomatic: When flourishing virtue rests in Water, the yu tone arises; it draws life from shang and takes jiao as its ally;

sentences.zh: 若用宮則刑，用徵則戰，故冬禁宮、徵。

translations.literal: if gong is used there will be punishments, if zhi is used there will be warfare—hence in winter gong and zhi are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: if gong is employed punishments follow, if zhi is employed warfare follows—therefore in winter gong and zhi are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 此三代之所共行，《月令》所載，深切著明者也。

translations.literal: This was practiced in common by the Three Dynasties, recorded in the Monthly Ordinances, clear and penetrating in its import.
translations.idiomatic: This practice was shared by the Three Dynasties and recorded in the Monthly Ordinances—plain, forceful, and unmistakable in meaning.

sentences.zh: 作樂本以導和，用失其宜，則反傷和氣。

translations.literal: Making music was originally meant to guide harmony; if used improperly, it instead harms the harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Music was created to lead all things toward harmony; used at the wrong season, it damages the harmonious qi instead.

sentences.zh: 夫淫哇殽雜，幹犯四時之氣久矣。

translations.literal: Licentious and vulgar sounds have long violated the qi of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Licentious and vulgar music has long transgressed against the qi of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 陛下親灑宸翰，發為詔旨，淫哇之聲轉為雅正，四時之禁亦右所頒，協氣則粹美，繹如以成。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally wielded the imperial brush and issued edicts; licentious sounds were transformed into orthodox refinement, and the seasonal prohibitions have also been promulgated—when qi harmonizes it becomes pure and perfect, continuous and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has personally taken up the imperial brush and issued edicts; licentious sounds are being turned to orthodox refinement, and the seasonal prohibitions have likewise been promulgated. When the qi aligns, purity and beauty follow, flowing on until the work is complete.

sentences.zh: ”詔令大晟府置圖頒降。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Great Sheng Prefecture to prepare diagrams and issue them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Great Sheng Prefecture to prepare illustrated charts and distribute them.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，大晟府言：“宴樂諸宮調多不正，如以無射為黃鍾宮，以夾鍾為中呂宮，以夷則為仙呂宮之類。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the Great Sheng Prefecture said: "Many modes of banquet music are incorrect, such as taking Wuyi as the Huangzhong gong, Jiazhong as the Zhonglü gong, Yize as the Xianlü gong, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Great Sheng Prefecture reported: "Many banquet modes are wrongly assigned—for example, treating Wuyi as the Huangzhong gong, Jiazhong as the Zhonglü gong, Yize as the Xianlü gong, and the like."

sentences.zh: 又加越調、雙調、大食、小食，皆俚俗所傳，今依月律改定。

translations.literal: Also added were Yuediao, Shuangdiao, Dashi, and Xiaoshi—all folk transmissions—now to be revised according to the monthly pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Yuediao, Shuangdiao, Dashi, and Xiaoshi were also added—all popular traditions—and are now to be corrected according to the monthly pitch standards.

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：“先帝嚐命儒臣肇造玉磬，藏之樂府，久不施用，其令略加磨礱，俾與律合。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict: "The late Emperor once ordered Confucian officials to first create jade chimes and store them in the Music Repository; they have long gone unused—order them lightly polished and trimmed so they accord with the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict declared: "The late Emperor once commanded Confucian scholars to cast jade chime-stones and store them in the Music Repository. They have long lain unused; let them be lightly polished and adjusted so they accord with the pitch pipes."

sentences.zh: 並造金鍾，專用於明堂。

translations.literal: Also cast golden bells, for exclusive use at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Golden bells shall also be cast, for exclusive use at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: ”又詔：“《大晟》雅樂，頃歲已命儒臣著樂書，獨宴樂未有紀述。

translations.literal: Another edict: "For Great Sheng ceremonial music, in recent years Confucian officials were already ordered to compile a music treatise, but banquet music alone has no record.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "For Great Sheng ceremonial music, Confucian scholars were already ordered in recent years to compile a music treatise, but banquet music alone has never been documented."

sentences.zh: 其令大晟府編集八十四調並圖譜，令劉昺撰以為《宴樂新書》。

translations.literal: Order the Great Sheng Prefecture to compile the eighty-four modes together with diagrams and registers, and have Liu Bing compose them into the New Book of Banquet Music.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Great Sheng Prefecture compile all eighty-four modes with diagrams and score-registers, and have Liu Bing compose them into the New Book of Banquet Music.

sentences.zh: ”十月，臣僚乞以崇寧、大觀、政和所得珍瑞名數，分命儒臣作為頌詩，協以新律，薦之郊廟，以告成功。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, officials requested that the rare omens obtained during Chongning, Daguan, and Zhenghe, by name and number, be assigned to Confucian officials to compose encomiastic poems, harmonized with the new pitch standards, and presented at the suburban altars and ancestral temples to proclaim success.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month officials requested that the rare omens recorded during Chongning, Daguan, and Zhenghe, item by item, be assigned to Confucian scholars to compose encomiastic poems set to the new pitch standards and offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples to proclaim the achievement.

sentences.zh: 詔送禮製局。

translations.literal: An edict referred the matter to the Bureau for Ritual Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Bureau for Ritual Regulations.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，典樂裴宗元言：“乞按習《虞書》賡載之歌，夏《五子之歌》，商之《那》，周之《關雎》、《麟趾》、《騶虞》、《鵲巢》、《鹿鳴》、《文王》、《清廟》之詩。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, Music Director Pei Zongyuan said: "We request rehearsal of the responsive song from the Book of Yu, the Xia 'Song of the Five Sons,' the Shang 'Na,' and the Zhou poems 'Guanju,' 'Linzhi,' 'Zouyu,' 'Quechao,' 'Luming,' 'Wenwang,' and 'Qingmiao.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year Pei Zongyuan, Director of Music, memorialized: "We request that the following be rehearsed: the responsive song from the Book of Yu, the Xia 'Song of the Five Sons,' the Shang 'Na,' and the Zhou poems 'Guanju,' 'Linzhi,' 'Zouyu,' 'Quechao,' 'Luming,' 'Wenwang,' and 'Qingmiao.'"

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 中書省言：“高麗，賜雅樂，乞習教聲律、大晟府撰樂譜辭。

translations.literal: The Secretariat said: "Goryeo, having been granted ceremonial music, requests instruction in pitch and mode; the Great Sheng Prefecture should compile musical scores and texts.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "Goryeo, having received ceremonial music as a gift, requests instruction in pitch and mode. The Great Sheng Prefecture should compile musical scores and texts."

sentences.zh: ”詔許教習，仍賜樂譜。

translations.literal: An edict permitted instruction and additionally granted musical scores.
translations.idiomatic: An edict authorized instruction and additionally granted musical scores.

sentences.zh: 三月，議禮局言：“先王之製，舞有小大：文舞之大，用羽、籥；

translations.literal: In the third month, the Bureau for Discussion of Rites said: "The institutions of the ancient kings distinguished great and small dances: the great civil dance used feathers and yue flutes;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Bureau for Discussion of Rites reported: "The ancient kings distinguished great and small dances. The great civil dance used feathers and yue flutes;

sentences.zh: 文舞之小，則有羽無籥，謂之羽舞。

translations.literal: the small civil dance had feathers but no yue flutes, called the feather dance.
translations.idiomatic: the small civil dance had feathers but no yue flutes and was called the feather dance.

sentences.zh: 武舞之大，用幹、戚；

translations.literal: The great martial dance used shield-staffs and battle-axes;
translations.idiomatic: The great martial dance used shield-staffs and battle-axes;

sentences.zh: 武舞之小，則有幹無戚，謂之幹舞。

translations.literal: the small martial dance had shield-staffs but no battle-axes, called the staff dance.
translations.idiomatic: the small martial dance had shield-staffs but no battle-axes and was called the staff dance.

sentences.zh: 武又有戈舞焉，而戈不用於大舞。

translations.literal: In martial dance there was also the halberd dance, but halberds were not used in the great dance.
translations.idiomatic: Martial dance also included the halberd dance, but halberds were not used in the great dance.

sentences.zh: 近世武舞以戈配幹，未嚐用戚。

translations.literal: In recent times the martial dance paired halberds with shield-staffs and never used battle-axes.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the martial dance paired halberds with shield-staffs and never employed battle-axes.

sentences.zh: 乞武舞以戚配幹，置戈不用，庶協古製。

translations.literal: We request that the martial dance pair battle-axes with shield-staffs and set aside halberds, so as to accord with ancient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the martial dance pair battle-axes with shield-staffs and set halberds aside, so as to accord with ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 又言：“ 伶州鳩曰：‘大鈞有鎛無鍾，鳴其細也；

translations.literal: Also submitted: "Ling Zhoujiu said: 'The great pitch-set has bell-chimes but no bells, to sound the fine tones;
translations.idiomatic: They also submitted: "Ling Zhoujiu said: 'The great pitch-set has bell-chimes but no bells, to give voice to the finer tones;

sentences.zh: 細鈞有鍾無鎛，昭其大也。

translations.literal: the fine pitch-set has bells but no bell-chimes, to proclaim the great tones.'
translations.idiomatic: the fine pitch-set has bells but no bell-chimes, to proclaim the greater tones.'"

sentences.zh: ’然則鍾，大器也；

translations.literal: 'Thus bells are great instruments;
translations.idiomatic: 'Thus bells are great instruments;

sentences.zh: 鎛，小鍾也。

translations.literal: bell-chimes are small bells.'
translations.idiomatic: bell-chimes are small bells.'

sentences.zh: 以宮、商為鈞，則謂之大鈞，其聲大，故用鎛以鳴其細，而不用鍾；

translations.literal: When gong and shang form the pitch-set, it is called the great pitch-set; its sound is great, hence bell-chimes are used to sound the fine tones and bells are not used;
translations.idiomatic: When gong and shang form the pitch-set, it is called the great pitch-set. Its sound is great, so bell-chimes are used to sound the finer tones and bells are not used;

sentences.zh: 以角、徵、羽為鈞，則謂之小鈞，其聲細，故用鍾以昭其大，而不用鎛。

translations.literal: when jiao, zhi, and yu form the pitch-set, it is called the fine pitch-set; its sound is fine, hence bells are used to proclaim the great tones and bell-chimes are not used.
translations.idiomatic: when jiao, zhi, and yu form the pitch-set, it is called the fine pitch-set. Its sound is fine, so bells are used to proclaim the greater tones and bell-chimes are not used.

sentences.zh: 然後細大不逾，聲應相保，和平出焉。

translations.literal: Only then do fine and great not exceed each other, sounds respond and sustain one another, and harmony emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Only then do fine and great remain within bounds, sounds answer and sustain one another, and harmony emerges.

sentences.zh: 是鎛、鍾兩器，其用不同，故周人各立其官。

translations.literal: Thus the two instruments, bell-chimes and bells, have different uses—hence the Zhou people established separate offices for each.
translations.idiomatic: Bell-chimes and bells are two instruments with distinct uses; that is why the Zhou established separate offices for each.

sentences.zh: 後世之鎛鍾，非特不分大小，又混為一器，復於樂架編鍾、編磬之外，設鎛鍾十二，配十二辰，皆非是。

translations.literal: Later ages' 'bell-chime bells' not only failed to distinguish great and small but mixed them into a single instrument; moreover, beyond the set bells and set chimes on the music frame, twelve 'bell-chime bells' were set up to match the twelve branches—all of which is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Later 'bell-chime bells' not only failed to distinguish great from small but conflated them into one instrument. Beyond the set bells and set chimes on the music frame, twelve 'bell-chime bells' were also installed to match the twelve branches—all of which is wrong.

sentences.zh: 蓋鎛鍾猶之特磬，與編鍾、編磬相須為用者也。

translations.literal: Bell-chimes are like the single chime stone—they depend on set bells and set chimes for use.
translations.idiomatic: Bell-chimes are like the single chime stone: they are meant to work in concert with set bells and set chimes.

sentences.zh: 編鍾、編磬，其陽聲六，以應律；

translations.literal: Set bells and set chimes: their six yang tones respond to the pitch pipes;
translations.idiomatic: Set bells and set chimes have six yang tones to answer the pitch pipes;

sentences.zh: 其陰聲六，以應呂。

translations.literal: their six yin tones respond to the pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: their six yin tones to answer the pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 既應十二辰矣，復為鎛鍾十二以配之，則於義生復。

translations.literal: Since they already respond to the twelve branches, to set up twelve bell-chime bells to match them is redundant in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Since they already answer the twelve branches, adding twelve bell-chime bells to match them is redundant in principle.

sentences.zh: 乞宮架樂去十二鎛鍾，止設一大鍾為鍾、一小鍾為鎛、一大磬為特磬，以為眾聲所依。

translations.literal: We request that palace-frame music remove the twelve bell-chime bells and set up only one great bell as the bell, one small bell as the bell-chime, and one great chime as the single chime stone, as the foundation for all sounds.
translations.idiomatic: We request that palace-frame music remove the twelve bell-chime bells and install only one great bell as the bell, one small bell as the bell-chime, and one great chime as the single chime stone—the foundation on which all other sounds depend.

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 四月，禮製局言：“尊祖配天者，郊祀也；

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Bureau for Ritual Regulations said: "Honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven—this is the suburban sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Bureau for Ritual Regulations reported: "Honoring the ancestor and pairing him with Heaven is the suburban sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 嚴父配天者，明堂也。

translations.literal: venerating the father and matching Heaven—this is the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: venerating the father and pairing him with Heaven is the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 所以來天神而禮之，其義一也。

translations.literal: The purpose of summoning and honoring the celestial gods is one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: Both rites summon the celestial gods to receive worship, and their meaning is one.

sentences.zh: 則明堂宜同郊祀，用禮天神六變之樂，其宮架赤紫，用雷鼓、雷鞀。

translations.literal: Thus the Bright Hall should follow the suburban sacrifice, using the six-transformations music for honoring the celestial gods; its palace frame should be red and purple, using thunder drums and thunder tambourines.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall should therefore follow the suburban sacrifice, using the six-transformations music for honoring the celestial gods. Its palace frame should be red and purple, with thunder drums and thunder tambourines.

sentences.zh: 又圜丘方澤，各有大樂宮架，自來明堂就用大慶殿大朝會宮架。

translations.literal: Also, the Round Mound and Square Pond each have great-music palace frames; from the outset the Bright Hall has used the grand court-assembly palace frame of Dafeng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Round Mound and Square Pond each have their own great-music palace frames, whereas the Bright Hall has from the first used the grand court-assembly palace frame of Dafeng Hall.

sentences.zh: 今明堂肇建，欲行創置。

translations.literal: Now that the Bright Hall is newly built, we wish to undertake a fresh establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Bright Hall is newly erected, we wish to establish a proper frame of its own.

sentences.zh: 十月，皇帝御明堂平朔左個，始以天運政治頒於天下。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall's Ping Shuo left bay and for the first time promulgated the calendar of Heaven's revolutions and governance throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor took his seat at the Ping Shuo left bay of the Bright Hall and for the first time promulgated the calendar of Heaven's revolutions and governance throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 是月也，凡樂之聲，以應鍾為宮、南呂為商、林鍾為角、仲呂為閏徵、姑洗為徵、太簇為羽、黃鍾為閏宮。

translations.literal: That month, for all music the tones were: Yingzhong as gong, Nanlü as shang, Linzhong as jiao, Zhonglü as intercalary zhi, Guxian as zhi, Taicu as yu, Huangzhong as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: That month, for all music Yingzhong served as gong, Nanlü as shang, Linzhong as jiao, Zhonglü as intercalary zhi, Guxian as zhi, Taicu as yu, and Huangzhong as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 既而中書省言：“五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮，若以左旋取之，如十月以應鍾為宮，則南呂為商、林鍾為角、仲呂為閏徵、姑洗為徵、太簇為羽、黃鍾為閏宮；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat said: "The five tones, six pitch standards, and twelve pipes cycle as gong-tonics; if taken by left rotation, as in the tenth month with Yingzhong as gong, then Nanlü is shang, Linzhong is jiao, Zhonglü is intercalary zhi, Guxian is zhi, Taicu is yu, Huangzhong is intercalary gong;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Secretariat reported: "The five tones, six pitch standards, and twelve pipes rotate as gong-tonics. By left rotation—for example, in the tenth month with Yingzhong as gong—Nanlü is shang, Linzhong jiao, Zhonglü intercalary zhi, Guxian zhi, Taicu yu, and Huangzhong intercalary gong;

sentences.zh: 若以右旋七均之法，如十月以應鍾為宮，則當用大呂為商、夾鍾為角、仲呂為閏徵、蕤賓為徵、夷則為羽、無射為閏宮。

translations.literal: if by the right-rotation seven-scale method, as in the tenth month with Yingzhong as gong, then Dalü should be shang, Jiazhong jiao, Zhonglü intercalary zhi, Ruibin zhi, Yize yu, Wuyi intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: by the right-rotation seven-scale method—for example, in the tenth month with Yingzhong as gong—Dalü should be shang, Jiazhong jiao, Zhonglü intercalary zhi, Ruibin zhi, Yize yu, and Wuyi intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 明堂頒朔，用左旋取之，非是。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall calendar promulgation used left rotation—this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall calendar promulgation used left rotation, which is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 欲以本月律為宮，右旋取七均之法。

translations.literal: We wish to take this month's pitch standard as gong and apply the right-rotation seven-scale method.
translations.idiomatic: We propose to take this month's pitch standard as gong and apply the right-rotation seven-scale method.

sentences.zh: ”從之，仍改正詔書行下。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted, and the revised edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was accepted, and a corrected edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 自是而後，樂律隨月右旋。

translations.literal: From then on, musical pitch standards rotated rightward with the month.
translations.idiomatic: From that point forward, musical pitch standards rotated rightward with the month.

sentences.zh: 仲冬之月，皇帝御明堂，南面以朝百辟，退，坐於平朔，授民時。

translations.literal: In the mid-winter month, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall, facing south to hold court with all officials; then retiring, he sat at Ping Shuo and granted the people the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-winter the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall, facing south to receive the hundred officials. Retiring afterward, he sat at Ping Shuo and granted the people their seasons.

sentences.zh: 樂以黃鍾為宮、太簇為商、姑洗為角、蕤賓為閏徵、林鍾為徵、南呂為羽、應鍾為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Huangzhong as gong, Taicu as shang, Guxian as jiao, Ruibin as intercalary zhi, Linzhong as zhi, Nanlü as yu, Yingzhong as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Huangzhong as gong, Taicu as shang, Guxian as jiao, Ruibin as intercalary zhi, Linzhong as zhi, Nanlü as yu, and Yingzhong as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 調以羽，使氣適平。

translations.literal: Tuned to yu, so the qi would be properly balanced.
translations.idiomatic: The mode was tuned to yu so the qi would settle into balance.

sentences.zh: 季冬之月，禦明堂平朔右個。

translations.literal: In late winter, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall's Ping Shuo right bay.
translations.idiomatic: In late winter the Emperor presided at the Ping Shuo right bay of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂以大呂為宮、夾鍾為商、仲呂為角、林鍾為閏徵、夷則為徽、無射為羽、黃鍾為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Dalü as gong, Jiazhong as shang, Zhonglü as jiao, Linzhong as intercalary zhi, Yize as zhi, Wuyi as yu, Huangzhong as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Dalü as gong, Jiazhong as shang, Zhonglü as jiao, Linzhong as intercalary zhi, Yize as zhi, Wuyi as yu, and Huangzhong as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 客氣少陰火，調以羽，尚羽而抑徵。

translations.literal: Guest qi of lesser yin fire—tune to yu, prioritize yu and suppress zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Guest qi of lesser yin fire: the mode was tuned to yu, emphasizing yu and suppressing zhi.

sentences.zh: 孟春之月，禦明堂青陽左個。

translations.literal: In early spring, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall's Qingyang left bay.
translations.idiomatic: In early spring the Emperor presided at the Qingyang left bay of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂以太簇為宮、姑洗為商、蕤賓為角、夷則為閏徵、南呂為徵、應鍾為羽、大呂為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Taicu as gong, Guxian as shang, Ruibin as jiao, Yize as intercalary zhi, Nanlü as zhi, Yingzhong as yu, Dalü as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Taicu as gong, Guxian as shang, Ruibin as jiao, Yize as intercalary zhi, Nanlü as zhi, Yingzhong as yu, and Dalü as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 客氣少陽相火，與歲運同，火氣太過，調宜羽，致其和。

translations.literal: Guest qi of lesser yang minister fire, identical with the year's dominant qi—fire qi is excessive; the mode should be tuned to yu to restore harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Guest qi of lesser yang minister fire coincided with the year's dominant qi; fire was excessive, so the mode was tuned to yu to restore harmony.

sentences.zh: 仲春之月，禦明堂青陽。

translations.literal: In mid-spring, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall's Qingyang hall.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-spring the Emperor presided at the Qingyang hall of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂以夾鍾為宮、仲呂為商、林鍾為角、南呂為閏徵、無射為徵、黃鍾為羽、太簇為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Jiazhong as gong, Zhonglü as shang, Linzhong as jiao, Nanlü as intercalary zhi, Wuyi as zhi, Huangzhong as yu, Taicu as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Jiazhong as gong, Zhonglü as shang, Linzhong as jiao, Nanlü as intercalary zhi, Wuyi as zhi, Huangzhong as yu, and Taicu as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 調以羽。

translations.literal: Tuned to yu.
translations.idiomatic: The mode was tuned to yu.

sentences.zh: 季春之月，禦明堂青陽右個。

translations.literal: In late spring, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall's Qingyang right bay.
translations.idiomatic: In late spring the Emperor presided at the Qingyang right bay of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂以姑洗為宮、蕤賓為商、夷則為角、無射為閏徵、應鍾為徵、大呂為羽、夾鍾為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Guxian as gong, Ruibin as shang, Yize as jiao, Wuyi as intercalary zhi, Yingzhong as zhi, Dalü as yu, Jiazhong as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Guxian as gong, Ruibin as shang, Yize as jiao, Wuyi as intercalary zhi, Yingzhong as zhi, Dalü as yu, and Jiazhong as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 客氣陽明，尚徵以抑金。

translations.literal: Guest qi of yang brilliance—prioritize zhi to suppress Metal.
translations.idiomatic: Guest qi of yang brilliance: zhi was emphasized to restrain Metal.

sentences.zh: 孟夏之月，禦明堂左個。

translations.literal: In early summer, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall's left bay.
translations.idiomatic: In early summer the Emperor presided at the left bay of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂以仲呂為宮、林鍾為商、南呂為角、應鍾為閏徵、黃鍾為徵、太簇為羽、姑洗為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Zhonglü as gong, Linzhong as shang, Nanlü as jiao, Yingzhong as intercalary zhi, Huangzhong as zhi, Taicu as yu, Guxian as intercalary gong.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Zhonglü as gong, Linzhong as shang, Nanlü as jiao, Yingzhong as intercalary zhi, Huangzhong as zhi, Taicu as yu, and Guxian as intercalary gong.

sentences.zh: 調宜尚徵。

translations.literal: The mode should emphasize zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The mode should emphasize zhi.

sentences.zh: 仲夏之月，禦明堂。

translations.literal: In mid-summer, the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-summer the Emperor presided at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 樂以蕤賓為宮、夷則為商、無射為角、黃鍾為閏徵、大呂為徵、夾鍾為羽、仲呂為閏宮。

translations.literal: Music: Ruibin as gong, Yize as shang, Wuyi as jiao, Huangzhong as intercalary zhi, Dalü as zhi, Jiazhong as yu, Zhonglü as intercalary gong.

translations.idiomatic: In mid-autumn the Emperor presided at the Zongzhang hall of the Bright Hall.

translations.idiomatic: In late autumn the Emperor presided at the Zongzhang right bay of the Bright Hall.

translations.literal: Music: Wuyi as gong, Huangzhong as shang, Taicu as jiao, Guxian as intercalary zhi, Zhonglü as zhi, Linzhong as yu, Nanlü as intercalary gong.
